Title: Constable Muhammad Raimi laid to rest after electric shock tragedy
Article:
DUNGUN: Constable Muhammad Raimi Ismarubee who was believed to have died from an electric shock in Kampung Weston, Beaufort, Sabah yesterday, was laid to rest at the Felda Kerteh 2 Muslim Cemetery here at 1.15 am today.
The vehicle carrying the late Muhammad Raimi, 24, arrived at his residence in Felda Kerteh 2 at 11.40pm for the final respects and funeral prayers before the burial.
Earlier, Muhammad Raimi's body was flown from Kota Kinabalu International Airport (KKIA), Sabah, aboard a Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) aircraft, which arrived at Kuantan Air Base, Pahang, before he was taken by hearse to Felda Kerteh 2.
The funeral prayers for the late Muhammad Raimi were led by Terengganu State Education, Higher Education, Science, Technology and Human Development Committee chairman Datuk Satiful Bahari Mamat.
Among those who attended the funeral were Dungun District Police Chief Supt Nik Ab Halim Nik Mat, about 200 officers and police personnel, as well as family members and friends of the late Muhammad Raimi.
The late Muhammad Raimi, who was still single, was the second of three siblings and began serving at the Weston Police Station in September 2024.
In the incident at 5.50 pm, three police personnel were confirmed dead after they were believed to have suffered electric shocks at Jalan Weston, Kampung Weston.
Muhammad Raimi and his two colleagues from the Weston Police Station, Corporal Chiu Teck Siong, 40, and Corporal Mohamad Nur Hafiz Ibrahim, 29, were the three personnel killed in the incident
–BERNAMA

Title: US Senate passes sweeping Russia sanctions bill
Article:
WASHINGTON: The US Senate on Friday passed a sweeping sanctions package targeting Russia's energy revenues.
The legislation now heads to the House of Representatives, though a vote there will not take place until at least early September due to the congressional summer recess.
"This could finally bring Russia to the negotiating table and end this conflict" between Russia and Ukraine, said Republican Jim Risch, chairman of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee.
"It will make a decisive impact that goes beyond what can be achieved on the battlefield. It will cut off the flow of cash that powers Putin's war machine," he added in a speech on the Senate floor before the vote.
The bill aims to target the Russian energy sector by imposing tariffs of up to 500 percent on imports from Russia, including gas and oil.
It also includes 100-per cent tariffs on the five main importing countries of Russian gas and oil, including China and India.
New sanctions against Russian President Vladimir Putin and other high-ranking officials are also to be imposed.
For the first time, the United States is also targeting Russia's shadow fleet, a clandestine network of ships used by Moscow to circumvent Western embargoes since the 2022 invasion of Ukraine.
'PRESSURE' ON PUTIN
The bill was named in honor of Lindsey Graham, the Republican senator who died on July 11 and who had strongly advocated for new sanctions against Moscow because of its invasion of Ukraine.
The day before his death, Graham, along with other Republican and Democratic senators, announced that they had secured the White House's approval to pass these new sanctions on Russian hydrocarbons, measures that had previously been blocked by President Donald Trump.
His sister, Darline Graham, who succeeded him in the Senate, said Friday the bill "hits Putin where it hurts."
Democratic Senator Jeanne Shaheen, a member of the Foreign Affairs Committee, said in a statement that the bill sent "Vladimir Putin an unambiguous and bipartisan message in the only language he understands: pressure."
RESERVATIONS IN THE HOUSE
According to Democratic Senator Raphael Warnock, Trade Representative Jamieson Greer finally gave assurances that countries among the top five buyers of Russian oil and gas would no longer be penalized if they dropped in the rankings to sixth or lower.
Several House members nevertheless expressed reservations about the bill, suggesting that passage in the lower chamber could be more difficult than in the Senate.
These new tariff powers could be used without restraint by Trump, Democratic Representatives Gregory Meeks and Don Beyer stated in a joint press release, calling the version adopted on Friday "unacceptable."
The head of the European Commission, Ursula von der Leyen, welcomed the passage of the bill.
"Together, let us drain Russia's means to continue a war it cannot win," she wrote on X.
The Russian Embassy in Washington last month condemned the legislation.
Given the war in Iran, "with an impending energy crisis and rising gas prices on the eve of the midterm elections, sanctioning Russia and its trading partners... would be extremely counterproductive for the United States," the embassy stated in a press release.

Title: Beyond fines: Demanding real accountability for social security exploitation
Article:
LETTERS:
The news that at least 100 people face fraud charges over bogus claims under Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) Daya Kerjaya 2.0 programme is deeply troubling.
What makes this case so serious is not just the scale — an estimated RM45 million in losses — but the source of the money.
These are contributions made by ordinary working people, from their wages, to fund protection and support they have earned through honest labour.
This fraud is not just an offence against the state; it is theft from every worker who pays into the system in good faith.
These funds are meant to serve those who need them most: people with disabilities, older workers, and others seeking help to secure work or improve their lives.
Instead, syndicates and dishonest employers allegedly used stolen personal data to submit fake claims, leaving many entitled people with only small, one-off payments—or nothing at all.
This is a gross betrayal of trust. Those who exploit social security systems treat workers' hard-earned contributions as easy pickings, and such behaviour must never be excused or downplayed.
Perkeso must now put far stronger safeguards in place. The fact that over 1,600 companies were under investigation shows the gaps were wide.
Better verification, stricter audits, and real-time checks on claims and beneficiaries are essential.
A single integrity officer is a start — but it is not enough. Systems must be tightened so that fraud is harder to attempt, easier to detect early, and far riskier to try.
Above all, punishment must be a true deterrent. If penalties are light, fraudsters will keep exploiting the system.
The courts must impose penalties that match the harm done: not just fines, but meaningful sentences that send a clear message.
Stealing from workers' social security is not a minor offence. When people cheat the system, they cheat us all.
TAN SRI LEE LAM THYE
Kuala Lumpur

Title: Selangor targets RM600b economy
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Selangor aims to grow its economy to   RM600 billion  by 2030 under its second five-year development plan, which seeks to  strengthen  the state's position  as Malaysia's economic powerhouse  while creating more high-paying jobs for its people.
Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said the state, which contributes 26.5 per cent to Malaysia's gross domestic product (GDP), would pursue a more ambitious growth strategy under the Second Selangor Plan (RS2) 2026-2030.
He said Selangor's economy is currently valued at RM460.1 billion and it aims to become the first in the country to achieve a RM500 billion economy.
"We are confident that during the Second Selangor Plan, the value of Selangor's economy can reach RM600 billion," he said when tabling the RS2 motion at the Selangor State Legislative Assembly yesterday.
Amirudin said achieving the target would require the state to move beyond "business as usual", particularly amid geopolitical uncertainty, rapid technological change and the emergence of artificial intelligence (AI).
RS2 comprises six missions,  25 priority areas and  98 initiatives covering economic growth, public transport, housing, household income, climate resilience and digital government.
[[nid:1506514]]
FIVE SECTORS DRIVE GROWTH
Under the first mission, he said the state would focus on five economic sectors — electrical and electronics, aerospace, automotive, digital and creative — through 13 initiatives.
The initiatives aim to sustain   economic and GDP growth at an average of  6.1 per cent over the five years, attract a total of RM330 billion in  investment  and reduce unemployment to 2.2 per cent by 2030.
Under the electrical and electronics sector, the second phase of the Integrated Circuit (IC)  Design Park would be expanded, with a target of creating 800 high-paying jobs for Selangor engineers.
The broader semiconductor ecosystem is expected to create 10,000 jobs by 2030, with the state seeking to move into higher-value activities and enable Selangor-based companies to own intellectual property for integrated circuit design.
In aerospace, Selangor, which accounts for more than 67 per cent of Malaysia's aerospace activities, would accelerate the Selangor Aero Park @ KLIA Aeropolis and Subang Airport Regeneration Plan.
The initiatives are expected to boost logistics, maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO), aircraft equipment manufacturing, and technical and vocational education and training (TVET).
For the automotive sector, Hulu Selangor is earmarked as a major hub through the Lembah Beringin High Tech Auto Valley, including for electric vehicle manufacturing.
Meanwhile, the digital and creative economies would be accelerated through the Selangor Digital Future Action Plan 2030 and the Selangor Creative Economy Advancement Hub.
Amirudin said the state would also strengthen small and medium enterprises  and help local companies expand into markets across Southeast Asia and Asia.
TRANSPORT AND HOUSING
Under the second mission, the state aims to increase public transport usage to at least 60 per cent from the current 40 per cent.
Amirudin said demand-responsive transit (DRT) services under Selangor Mobility would be recalibrated to focus on transporting people to commercial areas, while increasing bus stations'  connectivity  with LRT and MRT stations.
The state also plans to create more "walkable cities", including building  covered   walkways extending at least 500m from   rail  stations.
Selangor is targeting to build  200,000 affordable housing units for residents who do not own homes.
To date, 64,188 units have been completed and another 69,014 are under construction, bringing the total to 133,202 units.
For those unable to secure bank financing, the state plans to increase rental units under the Smart Sewa scheme to 3,000 by 2030.
HIGHER INCOMES, STRONGER SKILLS
Amirudin said the median monthly household income in Selangor had reached RM10,726, exceeding the RM9,290 target  under the first Selangor Plan.
Under RS2, the state aims to raise the figure to RM14,500 by 2030 while reducing unemployment to 2.2 per cent and maintaining GDP growth at 6.1 per cent.
He said the state would establish the Selangor Employment Skills Council to address mismatches between graduates' skills and industry requirements.
The state would also formalise the care economy and increase women's workforce participation through initiatives like  the Career Comeback Programme for mothers returning to work.
Its TVET framework, led by the Selangor Technical Skills Development Centre (STDC), would also be strengthened through  proposed corporatisation.
Amirudin said the state would expand the People's Tuition Programme (PTRS) to 200,000 students by 2030 and establish the Selangor University Network Council to strengthen collaboration between public and private universities.
GREEN GROWTH, WATER SECURITY
By 2035, the state aims to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 35 per cent against the 2005 baseline, while maintaining 31 per cent of its land area as gazetted forest reserve.
The Selangor Flood Mitigation Plan (SelFMiP)  would incorporate climate risks into district development and planning.
The state also plans to develop an integrated climate data management system, combining disaster, hydrological and geospatial data to improve early warning and disaster response.
Two waste-to-energy plants at Tanjung Duabelas and the Sultan Idris Shah Green Energy in Rawang are expected to process 2,400 tonnes of waste daily and generate 58 megawatts of electricity.
The state is also exploring nuclear energy to diversify its long-term energy mix and reduce dependence on external sources vulnerable to geopolitical disruptions.
Amirudin said water security would remain a priority, with five major infrastructure projects, including the Rasau Water Treatment Plant Phases One and Two, Langat 2 Phase Two and Labohan Dagang Phase Two.
DIGITAL GOVERNMENT, INVESTMENT REFORMS
The state targets all 12 local authorities achieving a  Local Authority Star Rating of 95 per cent or higher by 2030.
It will also accelerate end-to-end digital government services, with an 85 per cent target for digital government service-sharing.
The state government also aims to have  85 per cent  of its   services going totally digital.
Amirudin said the state would establish an integrated state holding investment company to diversify revenue streams and reduce its dependence on land premiums and quit rent, which currently account for about 75 per cent of state revenue.
He said   RS2 is anchored on  justice, which he describes as a development strategy rather than merely a moral aspiration.
"Justice produces trust. Trust produces confidence. Confidence produces investment. Investment produces jobs. Jobs produce dignity. And dignity produces a society that is confident about its future," he said.
Amirudin said the RS2 was more than a five-year development plan; it represents Selangor's commitment to investing in knowledge, research, innovation and human capital while ensuring economic growth was accompanied by social justice.
He said the state  aspires  to be an Asean model state by 2030, with an equitable economy, quality of life for all and a society confident in its future.

Title: PKR urged to confront hard truths after election setbacks [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR:  PKR must use its coming national congress for reflection in the wake of successive electoral defeats, an exodus from its ranks  and its deputy president's  taking leave.
Treasurer-general William Leong said the party, led by president Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim,  must  provide clarity over the issues that have plagued PKR since it came to power in Putrajaya and its plans to turn things around.
"There has been unhappiness, but it has now been translated into votes — or rather, no votes.
"It is time for members to get the party to reflect on the shortcomings," he told the
New Straits Times
.
[[nid:1506526]]
PKR has been on the losing end in Sabah, Johor and Negri Sembilan, where the party has seen its seats in the three states diminish from 19 to just three.
At the same time,   the departure of Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli  in May  has seen     the party undergoing    its biggest split since Datuk Seri Mohamed Azmin Ali and his followers left during the Sheraton Move in 2020.
The exit of Rafizi  comes after his failure to defend his PKR deputy presidency in  a divisive party election in May last year. Another casualty of the polls was  former PKR vice-president Nik Nazmi Nik Ahmad. The duo have gone on to form Parti Bersama Malaysia, which has drawn a number of grassroots leaders.
Complicating matters is Nurul Izzah Anwar's decision to step down as deputy president to continue her studies. The resignation was rejected, with the party instead granting her temporary leave from her duties.
Leong said PKR grassroots must remain steadfast and united.
"The party is more than individuals, the party is more than leaders.
"Leaders will come and go, and the party will have to remain, and the members will have to stand together.
"Members must reflect on why they joined the party. It is for a cause, for reform, and for the betterment of the country."
Leaders, meanwhile, must listen to what the grassroots are saying, he said, adding that this was what the congress is about.
Pasir Gudang member of parliament Hassan Abdul Karim said PKR faced an existential threat following its electoral defeats and the exit of key reformist figures.
"PKR members are divided at this juncture. Many remain in the party out of continued faith in Anwar's leadership, but support and respect are slowly diminishing as capable leaders like Rafizi Ramli and Nik Nazmi have left, and now Nurul Izzah appears dissatisfied with the current situation in PKR and the government."
He said Anwar's best bet to revive support for PKR lay in translating macroeconomic policies into microeconomic benefits on the ground.
Analyst Asrul Sani of the Asia Group said the Aug 15-16 congress must serve as a "wake-up call" for the party.
"Being in the federal government has not automatically translated into stronger support on the ground, and the leadership cannot afford to treat these results as isolated setbacks," he said.
"Members   want to know whether the party understands the scale of the problem and whether it has a credible plan to reverse it."
Amid Rafizi's faction's departure and Nurul Izzah's leave of absence, Asrul said Anwar and PKR needed more than   loyalists.
"Institutionally, PKR has never been more powerful, with its president serving as prime minister and the party at the centre of the federal government. Politically, however, it risks appearing weaker and less energetic than it did when it was in opposition."
To remain relevant, Asrul said PKR must allow internal debate, strengthen grassroots engagement and decouple its political identity from Anwar.
"The major change has to be institutional.
"PKR needs to demonstrate that it can produce leaders, ideas and a political identity independent of Anwar," Asrul said.
He added that PKR needed to communicate better with members and supporters.
"PKR and Pakatan Harapan  now need to define what they stand for as governing political movements rather than continuing to rely on the narratives that sustained them in opposition."

Title: US appeals court orders halt to Trump ballroom construction
Article:
WASHINGTON: An appeals court dealt a blow to US President Donald Trump's prized White House ballroom project on Friday, upholding a judge's ruling that construction must halt since Congress had not approved it.
The appeals court, which had temporarily allowed construction to continue while it considered the case, upheld the lower court's ruling but stayed its own decision for two weeks, giving Trump time to ask the Supreme Court to intervene.
A three-judge panel of the US Court of Appeals for the DC Circuit ruled 2-1 to uphold the district court order to halt construction above ground, while allowing work to continue below ground, where a military bunker is planned.
"This holding has nothing at all to do with whether the proposed ballroom is desirable, or not, as a matter of policy. This ruling does not even necessarily mean that the Defendants may not ultimately construct the ballroom," the majority wrote.
"What it does mean is that the Defendants may not do so during the district court's expeditious litigation without securing Congress's authorisation, as the Constitution and laws require."
Trump, who has repeatedly complained that the White House lacks sufficient space for grand galas such as state dinners, unilaterally ordered construction of the massive ballroom.
Work on the project began last year with the sudden demolition of the White House's entire historic East Wing.
It is just one of Trump's pet projects to leave his mark on Washington by the time he leaves office in 2029, along with a renovation of the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool and other parks, as well as the construction of a gigantic arch.

Title: NST Leader: Stopping the theft of public funds
Article:
The government — through its agencies and statutory bodies — has come up with many programmes to bring some measure of relief  to   people hard done by circumstances.
These initiatives involve large sums from the public purse — i.e. money raised  from the taxpayer. These allocations, while substantial, are never enough, so it is essential that any leakages are plugged to ensure the funds reach the maximum number of people  who need them.
Unfortunately, these   allocations are irresistable to the corrupt seeking a quick buck. Ask most people on the street who is the  likely culprit siphoning public funds and the answer is more often than not "a government officer".
But let us not forget the unscrupulous in the  private sector.
In the latest scandal, 100 individuals will be charged for making false claims under the Social Security Organisation's Daya Kerjaya 2.0 programme, which is meant to incentivise employers to hire disadvantaged people such as those with disabilities, ex-convicts and senior citizens.
Involving directors of 143 companies and 320 workers, the fraud is based on suspected false claims of RM9.01 million in 2024.
False employee verification forms and information were submitted to claim incentives for unqualified workers.
A welfare programme to support vulnerable groups, encourage employment and help businesses overcome economic challenges has been subverted.
Funds were shamefully taken away from deserving jobseekers, employers and qualified families.
How to stop this exploitation? While the need for strong oversight, data sharing, regular audits, strong verification and swift enforcement are often cited, they are only good "after the fact".
There must be beefier preventive   policies to stop financial malfeasance.   The   exploitation of  administrative leakages, procedural weaknesses and  poor transparency to satiate an  infinite greed must be stamped out.
Anti-corruption efforts are often targeted at  civil servants, and this is understandable.
For years,  the rogues' gallery has been populated by errant government officers taking a nibble out of public allocations.
But let us not forget it is often corporate greed that greases the corrupt  machinations  of these officers. A reminder that inculcating integrity is a whole-of-nation effort, not just in the corridors of Putrajaya.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: US unexpectedly loses jobs in setback for Trump ahead of midterms
Article:
WASHINGTON: The United States unexpectedly lost thousands of jobs in July, government data showed Friday, a blow to US President Donald Trump's claims of leading an economic revival as his Republican party gears up for crucial midterm elections.
The world's largest economy lost 23,000 jobs in July, data published by the US Bureau of Labour Statistics showed, signalling potential labour market weakness after months of steady growth.
The unemployment rate ticked down to 4.1 per cent, likely a result of falling labour supply as the US economy grapples with an aging population and lower net migration.
Since taking office for his second term, Trump has unleashed a spate of policies aimed at reviving domestic manufacturing and curbing surging inflation.
Republicans face a stiff test in November's midterm elections, with the state of the economy a key issue for Democrats who are seeking to wrest back control of both houses of Congress.
Friday's data will also pose a question to the US Federal Reserve, which has been signalling it was preparing for a rate hike later this year.
- IMPLICATIONS FOR FED -
The bulk of the loss in July was attributed to the local government education sector, which sees thousands of teachers drop off payrolls in the summer months.
Still, analysts had expected overall job growth. Economists polled by Dow Jones Newswires and the Wall Street Journal anticipated 83,000 new jobs would be added in July.
The BLS also revised down job growth in the previous two months by 103,000, showing the labour market to be less robust than previously reported.
Based on the new figures, job growth hit a peak in March before declining in the next three months and entering negative territory in July.
White House economic advisor Kevin Hassett dismissed Friday's data as being based on a survey that is "very, very noisy."
The unemployment rate has remained relatively steady through choppiness in the labour market, due to the overall drop in labour supply.
Friday's figures showed the labour force participation rate – a key metric – had dropped to its lowest level since the height of pandemic-related closures.
Policymakers at the US Federal Reserve watch the labour market closely, as their dual mandate requires them to deliver maximum employment while ensuring inflation remains at a long-term target of two per cent.
The Fed has missed that target for five years, as inflation has battered US households since the pandemic.
Last month, the central bank held interest rates steady, but three regional Fed presidents dissented in favor of a rate hike.
"This morning's report is a game changer in the sense that all of the recent focus has been on inflation and this report highlights the risks that are embedded in the labour market as well," said Chris Zaccarelli of Northlight Asset Management.
Kathy Bostjancic, chief economist at Nationwide, said the Fed would not be swayed by a single job report from its inflation focus.
"The soft labour market report should lower market expectations for a Fed rate hike in the coming months, but the inflation reports will be the key focus for Fed officials," she said.
- WAGES LAG INFLATION -
Sector-wise, retail trade lost 19,000 jobs, with employment declining in warehouse retailers – firms like Costco, Sam's Club and others that offer discounts for wholesale quantities of household goods – and general merchandise stores.
Employment in the financial activities sector continued its downward trend, having lost 121,000 jobs from its May 2025 peak.
The health care sector has buoyed the US labour market over the last year, with more Americans aging and requiring medical assistance.
In July, the sector added 22,000 jobs, but it was a slower pace than its average gain over the last year.
Average hourly earnings increased by 3.2 per cent year-on-year, lagging inflation and therefore leaving workers with less income in real terms.
Diane Swonk, chief economist at KPMG, said persistent inflation and a potentially weak labour market could put the Fed in a tough spot when it meets to set rates next month.
"The worst combination for the Fed is if inflation remains sticky while the labour market weakens," she said.
"That would not take rate hikes off the table; it would make them more painful."--AFP

Title: Elderly man killed when BMW crashes into driving institute fence
Article:
MARANG: An elderly man was killed when the BMW he was driving skidded and crashed into the fence of a driving institute along Jalan Kuala Terengganu-Kuantan, near Alur Tuman, here on Friday.
District police chief Superintendent Mohd Sofian Redzuan said they received a call from the public regarding the accident in front of the driving institute at 7.30am.
He said initial investigations found that the 65-year-old victim was driving from Masjid Kelulut to his home in Pulau Kerengga when he lost control of the vehicle, causing it to veer onto the right shoulder of the road before crashing into the fence of the driving institute.
"The man was confirmed dead at the scene due to head injuries. The body was sent to Sultanah Nur Zahirah Hospital (HSNZ) for a post-mortem," he said when contacted.
He said the case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.

Title: Hamzah says party decisions do not represent PN position
Article:
PETALING JAYA: The views or decisions of an individual political party should not be regarded as representing Perikatan Nasional (PN), as the coalition is governed by its own constitution and decision-making mechanisms, said Parti Wawasan Negara (Wawasan) president Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin.
Hamzah said PN was a coalition comprising several political parties, each governed by its own constitution and internal procedures.
"There are different constitutions governing the respective parties, so the thinking or decisions of one party cannot simply be taken as the position of the coalition, because the coalition itself has its own constitution.
"For example, if there is a need to amend the PN constitution, the matter can be decided through a coalition meeting.
"For Wawasan, however, any amendment to the party constitution must be made through an extraordinary general meeting involving delegates. So the processes are different," he said at a press conference after Wawasan's extraordinary general meeting here.
Hamzah was responding to questions over Pas president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang's assertion that
Bersatu's membership in PN
had automatically lapsed following Bersatu president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin's announcement that the party would form a new coalition.
Earlier, Bersatu secretary-general Datuk Seri Mohamed Azmin Ali
rejected Hadi's assertion,
saying the PN constitution contained no provision for a member party's membership to lapse automatically.
In a separate development, Hamzah, who is also Larut member of parliament, said the meeting approved amendments to the constitution of the party, formerly known as Parti Cinta Malaysia.
He said the amendments included the introduction of a new political philosophy aimed at positioning the party as a platform for Malaysians, anchored in the Federal Constitution, the Rukun Negara and the practice of mature democracy.
"The new constitution contains 30 clauses, and all the proposed amendments were approved at the meeting.
"In addition, the party's Advisory Council, which will be chaired by Tan Sri Rais Yatim, will continue to serve in an advisory capacity alongside several other figures who will be appointed," he said.

Title: Khairul Aming hits RM2mil in 2 minutes in TikTok sales
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Influencer and entrepreneur Khairul Aming took just two minutes to rack up RM2 million in sales of his latest products on TikTok.
The 33-year-old made the announcement on TikTok Live from Menara Merdeka Maybank, where he held the launch of his products.
Among the new products was Rendang Nyet Berapi, Dendeng Nyet Ekstra Pedas and Oriental Kopi Putih Premium.
The live session garnered 300,000 views, triple that of a similar one last year.
The sales broke his personal record, reflecting the significant influence content creators have on digital sales.
As of 10.45pm, more than 50,000 products were sold.

Title: Speaker Johari: Wong Chen told me he wanted to resign as MP
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul says PKR's Wong Chen had voiced his intentions to resign as Subang member of parliament.
He said Wong had said this to him when they had met recently.
"He intends to resign as a member of parliament and stated the reasons behind this," he said in a brief reply to Berita Harian.
Johari, however, did not say whether Wong had submitted a resignation letter, as claimed in viral social media posts, nor did he say what reasons the PKR man had given.
The claims that Wong had resigned came about after he had posted a picture of the letterhead from his parliamentary service centre, addressed to the "Dewan Rakyat Speaker".
However, no further details were given.
Instead, the three-term MP only said he would issue a statement on Monday regarding the letter and his meeting with Johari.
"This morning, I had a longer than expected meeting with Tan Sri Johari, the Speaker of Dewan Rakyat. We were supposed to meet for 30 minutes but ended up talking for 1.5 hours.
"The important thing is, I delivered my letter to him. I will release a press statement next Monday," he posted.

Title: Widow never expected policeman husband to return home in a coffin
Article:
SIBU: Corporal Chiu Teck Siong's widow, Tan Wei Wei, 39, never imagined her husband would "return" earlier than his scheduled leave on Aug 27.
Instead, his return was marked by grief as their five daughters, aged four to 11, received his coffin.
Tan said Chiu had long wished to be transferred to Sibu so the family could live together.
"He had wanted to be transferred back here for a long time, but it never happened. I never expected he would return like this," she said at the Ching Chuan Sibu Mortuary Hall.
She added the last time Chiu spent time with his children was during Chinese New Year.
"What I am thinking about now is their future education. My income is not high; I hope there are those willing to help our family," she said.
Chiu, 40, was among three police personnel who died, believed to have been electrocuted, outside the Weston police station in Beaufort, Sabah, yesterday.
His remains were flown from Kota Kinabalu and arrived at Sibu Airport at 5.50pm. A final respects ceremony will be held tomorrow morning before cremation at Nirvana Memorial Park, with ashes later laid to rest at Methodist Grace Memorial Park.
The two other victims were Corporal Mohamad Nur Hafiz Ibrahim, 29, and Constable Muhammad Raimi Ismarubee, 26.– BERNAMA

Title: No rift between BN and PN, says Hamzah
Article:
PETALING JAYA: Parti Wawasan Negara president Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin has dismissed speculation of strained relations between Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN), describing such claims as attempts to sow division.
"I do not see any rift between PN and BN. We have only just been sworn in (in Negri Sembilan) today. How can people already say there is a rift?
"These are elements trying to divide us," he said at a press conference after the party's extraordinary general meeting here today.
Hamzah said he had also heard remarks by Pas president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang and maintained that there were no problems between the parties.
He also took a swipe at developments within PKR following deputy president Nurul Izzah Anwar's decision to step down from the post.
"This is a story created by other people. If another party (member) wants to resign from a position or do something else, that is their business.
"If we do not interfere in other people's affairs, I also ask others not to interfere with the blue wave," he said.
Hamzah said the "blue wave" was aimed at ensuring continued public support, with the broader agenda centred on serving the people.
"What is important politically is that the blue wave truly reflects our responsibility when we are in power.
"For example, if we have formed the state government, we should carry out what we promised during the campaign. We should not say one thing during the campaign and sound different after winning and coming to power.
"Whatever other parties want to do is their business. It has nothing to do with us," he added.

Title: Freelance host, businessman arrested for podcast episode that touched on 3R
Article:
KLANG: Police confirmed the arrest of two men following a report received regarding a podcast episode that allegedly touched on religious sensitivities.
Klang Utara police chief Assistant Commissioner Ramsay Embol said police received the report on Aug 5 before the arrests of a freelance host and a businessman, aged in their 30s and 60s respectively, were carried out yesterday.
"Police have received a report regarding a video clip of a podcast created by two individuals discussing the issues of secular and liberal ideologies.
"This video clip was uploaded onto social media platforms where the podcast content touches on religious issues involving elements of race, religion, and royalty (3R)," he said in a statement today.
Ramsay added that police are committed to conducting investigations professionally, transparently, and fairly, while advising the public not to make any speculations or spread information that could compromise the investigation process.
The case is being investigated under Sections 298, 504, and 505(b) of the Penal Code, Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998, and Section 4(1) of the Sedition Act 1948.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar: Party differences should not hinder friendship, cooperation for people's benefit
Article:
MELAKA: Differences in the political parties governing the federal and state governments should not stand in the way of friendship and cooperation between them, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
He said close ties and cooperation were essential to ensure the people continued to benefit from government initiatives.
"Our system of government requires close cooperation. We may have differing views and belong to different political parties, but these differences should not hinder friendship, goodwill and cooperation that directly benefit the people.
"That is why I would like to express my sincere appreciation and gratitude for the warm welcome in Melaka and the close cooperation extended by the Melaka government and the Melaka Historic City Council (MBMB).
"We hope that our aspiration to create a sustainable landscape in line with the Malaysia Madani concept will be translated into action and produce tangible results in the near future," he said.
He said this when officiating at the National Landscape Day celebration, themed 'Landskap Lestari, Malaysia Madani' (Sustainable Landscape, Malaysia Madani) at the Hang Jebat Stadium in Krubong here tonight.
Also present were Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh, Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming and Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar.
Meanwhile, Anwar said national development planning should take into account places frequented by the public, including the cleanliness of food stalls.
He said the relevant authorities should allocate dedicated funding for such efforts instead of focusing solely on mega projects that largely benefit higher-income groups.
"Yes, we are known for our impressive landmarks, but we must not forget that the majority of Malaysians do not dine at five-star restaurants. In Kuala Lumpur, about 80 per cent of the people eat at hawker stalls, roadside eateries and small restaurants.
"How much attention do we give to beautifying and keeping these places clean? That is why I say development planning will fail if we do not strike the right balance," he said.
The prime minister said development must be carried out in a balanced manner across all sectors to enhance the country's standing on the world stage.

Title: [UPDATED] Hamzah: BN, PN must compromise on Melaka seats to sustain 'Blue Wave'
Article:
PETALING JAYA: Perikatan Nasional and Barisan Nasional must be prepared to compromise on seat allocations in Melaka if they want to sustain the "Blue Wave" momentum, said Parti Wawasan Negara president Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin.
"If we truly want to come together, we have to look at the 'Blue Wave' that began in Johor and continued into Negri Sembilan.
"If we want to keep that wave going, we must have a spirit of compromise," Hamzah told reporters after the party's extraordinary general meeting here today.
His remarks came after BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the coalition intended to
defend all 21 seats
it currently held in the state, potentially leaving just seven of Melaka's 28 seats for its partners.
Hamzah said seat allocations would have to be discussed among the leaders of the parties involved, adding that it was only natural for each party to seek as many seats as possible.
"InsyaAllah, when it comes to the wishes of each party, of course everyone wants more.
"But when we look at the broader picture, it is not only about Melaka. We also have to take into account the situation in other states.
"That is when we will be able to reach compromises that can be sustained," he said.
Hamzah said Wawasan also intended to defend seats where its allies and supporters were already established, citing Bemban and Sungai Udang constituencies as examples.
"So, of course, we want to retain them, not merely so they can contest, but to ensure that they win the election," he added.

Title: Tesla's FSD secrecy raises troubling safety questions
Article:
FOUR months ago, the Netherlands approved Tesla's Full Self-Driving (FSD) system and has since then advocated for its adoption across the European Union.
But Dutch road regulator RDW won't tell the public why it concluded the driver-assistance system is safe or how it evaluated the technology, which for years has faced regulatory investigations and lawsuits over FSD-involved crashes in the United States.
Releasing such details would violate Tesla's commercial secrets, the regulator said, echoing the automaker's own demands on the regulator for confidentiality.
Since late 2024, Tesla has pressed RDW to keep documentation about the FSD safety review secret, according to previously unreported email correspondence between the Dutch regulator and Tesla, obtained through a public-records request.
Tesla has called FSD approval key to boosting sales in Europe, where it's trying to regain market share lost in recent years and faces fierce competition from Chinese electric vehicles.
European regulators have historically been more cautious about automated driving than the United States, requiring automakers to get approval before deploying driver-assistance systems such as FSD.
Tesla chief executive officer Elon Musk has repeatedly said FSD, which requires a human driver to pay strict attention, will soon be fully autonomous.
An investigation in May found that Tesla's self-published FSD safety statistics are highly exaggerated and the company is nowhere near releasing self-driving technology at scale.
It was reported in June that Tesla had shared inflated FSD safety data from the US with several EU regulators, including RDW, as it sought approval.
RDW said it did not rely on Tesla's statistics and did its own "extensive testing" on closed tracks and public roads, in various conditions, without specifying how it measured performance or safety.
European vehicle-safety law experts say RDW is withholding far too much information under the guise of trade secrets, potentially at the expense of public safety.
Details on RDW's testing and Tesla's performance are matters of broad public interest, said Oliver Carsten, a transportation-safety professor at the University of Leeds, who has been involved in crafting European automated-driving regulations.
"I don't see any reason why that couldn't be public," he said.
Frank Mutze, policy and project manager for the advocacy group European Transport Safety Council, said the public is left to trust that authorities "have done their homework, which of course isn't good enough for us".
RDW declined to say how it evaluated FSD safety testing or to release documents on the testing, citing an "obligation to protect manufacturer-specific information".
The agency did not explain how details of its testing or conclusions about the system's performance could reveal commercially sensitive information.
RDW announced in April that it had concluded FSD is "safer than other driver assistance systems".
In June, RDW said it is "at least as safe as other driver assistance systems". The agency offered no data or evidence supporting those statements.
RDW is now seeking EU approval for FSD, which requires a "yes" vote from representatives of 55 per cent of member states that make up 65 per cent of the bloc's population. A vote could happen in October.
Tesla made secrecy a priority throughout its application, according to correspondence between the automaker and the regulator beginning in late 2024.
In one example from April 2025, a Tesla representative sought to confirm RDW would "never" release a particular document and asked how it would ensure it was "withheld from public disclosure".
Tesla, the employee said, could not provide more information to RDW "until this matter is clarified".
RDW told Tesla that disclosure under public records law shouldn't be a problem because "manufacturers always have the option to request an exemption from disclosing certain information".
RDW said it has not withheld information at Tesla's request but rather makes its own decisions on how to protect company trade secrets.
Tesla has a history of trying to shield information it gives regulators from public view. In the United States, it petitions federal safety regulators to redact basic details about every crash involving its driver-assistance systems.
Other European regulators, who are getting some unspecified FSD testing information from RDW, have taken a similar line on confidentiality.
Regulators in six European countries including Germany, Norway and Denmark all told Reuters they could not release data on FSD testing or performance because of concerns about trade secrets.
The writers are from Reuters
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar announces RM1.29mil allocation for Melaka Islamic schools
Article:
ALOR GAJAH: The government has approved RM1.29 million for 13 maintenance and repair projects at Islamic education institutions (IPI), including Sekolah Agama Rakyat (SAR) under the Melaka Islamic Religious Department (Jaim) this year.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced the allocation while opening the Madani Wave Carnival at the Masjid Tanah Sports Complex here today.
He said the government was concerned about the condition of Islamic education institutions, including pondok schools and tahfiz centres nationwide, which had been neglected without funding, while also balancing assistance for Chinese and Indian schools.
The allocation would cover basic infrastructure repairs at pondok and tahfiz education centres, upgrades to school areas, resurfacing of reserve areas for use as parking spaces, as well as building repairs and repainting works.
"Of the total allocation, Madrasah Tahfidz Al-Quran Wal Qiraat in Kota Melaka received the largest amount of RM250,000 for basic infrastructure repair works at the pondok and tahfiz education centre.
"Other recipients include Sekolah Agama Rakyat (SAR) Jaim Durian Tunggal with RM140,000, SAR Jaim Tebong, Jasin (RM30,000), SAR Jaim Kampung Baru (RM50,000), SAR Jaim Serkam Darat (RM70,000) and SAR Jaim Taman Maju, Jasin (RM100,000)," he said in his speech.
The programme was also attended by the prime minister's wife, Datin Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail.
Also present were Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh and Deputy Higher Education Minister Adam Adly Abdul Halim.
Meanwhile, Anwar said the government would continue efforts to support and safeguard the interests of the country's multiracial communities.
"Once again, I would like to stress that for programmes and assistance for Chinese and Tamil schools, we have decided to make the announcement in Kuala Lumpur in two weeks.
"If this country wants peace, we must take care of everyone. Muslims are the majority, so the interests of the majority are provided for Islam. Children in pondok schools and maahad tahfiz have been neglected and received no assistance, so we are increasing support," he said.

Title: The AI boom's emerging market reality
Article:
A few years ago, when almost every bank research note seemed to focus on soaring United States tech stocks, veteran emerging market fund manager Carlos von Hardenberg was struggling to get investors interested in anything else. Not any more.
Now the artificial intelligence boom has lit a rocket under the South Korean and Taiwanese firms that dominate high-tech memory chip making and, as of this year, the global EM stock indexes that have emerged from Wall Street's shadow.
"Investors would say they were only interested in the US and Magnificent Seven, and this is all you need because they were doing so well," said Hardenberg, who co-founded MCP Emerging Markets in 2018 alongside pioneering EM bull Mark Mobius.
"Now this year, everything turned the other way around."
But riding the AI boom has come at a cost. Since late June extreme volatility has taken hold, almost as if investors suddenly got altitude sickness.
South Korea's KOSPI index, which had doubled in value on the back of even bigger gains for Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, ripped back 40 per cent in just six weeks on a mix of concerns and curbs.
Taiwan's TSMC, by far the biggest company in the EM stock universe, fell almost 14 per cent.
It sent volatility in South Korea skyrocketing and even for MSCI's US$1.8 trillion EM benchmark, which contains more than 1,175 companies from 24 different countries, it surpassed the peaks of the Covid-19 pandemic.
"The clients that we speak to, the institutional clients, are struggling with the level of volatility in Korea at the moment," said William Bratton, head of cash equity research for APAC at BNP Paribas.
For some, the risk of the recent mayhem is that all those old longings for some Mag 7-style excitement in EM become a classic case of "careful what you wish for".
Just nine companies—mostly the big Taiwanese and Korean tech firms, plus Alibaba and Tencent in China —now account for more than 40 per cent of MSCI EM, making it even more top heavy than the US index.
The Korean market's swings have even been larger than cryptocurrency bitcoin's this year, while the recent rout saw the most dramatic drop in the MSCI EM index's "liquidity factor" ever — a result, the firm's chief research officer says, of investors moving away from the shares that had been surging.
"What we're seeing is that emerging markets, which people used to look to as a source of diversification, because of the emergence and importance of these extremely large AI-related, particularly AI hardware-related companies, are not really a source of diversification anymore," MSCI's research head Ashley Lester said.
"They're right in the centre of the AI boom."
Ji Young Park, a portfolio manager at Europe's biggest fund manager Amundi, said she had started scaling back some of her exposure before the turbulence kicked off, but that the sell-off had still been costly.
"I think in the last month there have been six or seven circuit breakers (on the Korean stock market), so it tells you just how volatile it has been," Park said.
While giant lurches aren't necessarily a limiting factor for her fund, they do cause caution.
"That's not the kind of investor that I am because I'm trying to buy a stock over five years," Park added. "And I quite like to sleep at night."
UBP technology portfolio manager, Dimitri Kallianiotis, said some of his private bank clients have been spooked too, although his advice has been not to panic.
LSEG data shows that the too-big-too-fast factor meant international investors pulled money out of Asia-ex China share markets faster than during any six months going back to at least 2010 in the first half of the year.
South Korea and Taiwan bore the brunt, shedding over US$100 billion and US$44 billion respectively, according to JPMorgan, as rules designed to prevent funds holding too much of any one stock saw investors cash in some of the 12-month gains on Samsung and SK Hynix.
"Ride the volatility and try to avoid the overhyped names," UBP's Kallianiotis said. "If you are not invested in the tempest days, you won't be there for the rebound."
The writer is from Reuters

Title: Rauf: Melaka advances sustainable landscape development
Article:
MELAKA: Melaka has established a strong foundation for sustainable landscape development through the enforcement of the Tree Preservation Order under the Town and Country Planning Act 1976.
This, said Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh, safeguards high-value trees that form an integral part of the state's landscape heritage.
He said the introduction of the Melaka Landscape Guidelines in 2022 had further strengthened the foundation by providing a comprehensive framework for implementing agencies, local authorities, developers and stakeholders to undertake landscape development in a planned, high-quality, distinctive and sustainable manner.
"More importantly, Melaka is strengthening the digitalisation of landscape management through the development of the MyTrees@Melaka system, a state-led innovation that is transforming tree management into a more efficient, systematic and integrated process.
"Since its development in 2017, a total of 70,753 tree inventory records have been compiled up to 2026 through collaboration between the four local authorities and the Melaka Forestry Department," he said at the National Landscape Day 2026 celebration here tonight.
The event was officiated by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and was also attended by Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming.
Rauf said the state government had also continued to intensify its greening efforts, with a total of 10,588 trees successfully planted throughout Melaka as of last June.
He said, based on the future landscape management framework set by the state government, every tree planted must be recorded, monitored and maintained based on data, ensuring more efficient, safer and sustainable management practices.
He said building on the foundation that had been established, the state government was also realising the Aspiring Melaka Geopark as a link between geological heritage, biodiversity, culture and local identity, reflecting the uniqueness of Melaka.
He said the effort would ensure Melaka's landscape treasures were not only preserved but also leveraged as a platform for education, conservation and nature-based tourism that generates sustainable economic value for communities.
In the meantime, he said, three major landscape projects had been implemented in Melaka last year, namely the development of SDG Park @ Sungai Melaka, Kampung Felda Air Kangkung Recreation Park and Taman Kejiranan Pulai Indah.
"These efforts will continue this year through three additional Madani Recreational Park projects involving the upgrading of the Dataran Sejarah Ayer Keroh landscape, the Ayer Keroh Art Lanai and the Bukit Beringin Masjid Tanah Madani Recreational Park.
"These projects are not just about beautifying the areas, but about creating spaces that can be used and enjoyed by the people, demonstrating that progress is not only measured by physical development, but also by our ability to preserve the ecosystem and improve people's quality of life," he said.
Earlier, Rauf said the four-day National Landscape Day 2026 celebration, which started yesterday, attracted nearly 3,000 participants from across the country.
These, he said, included landscape architecture professionals, local authority representatives, industry players, academics and landscape enthusiasts, serving as a platform for collaboration, innovation and knowledge exchange.
He said a total of 12 local authority pavilions showcasing creativity, innovation and unique landscape identities were also developed, making the celebration a platform for sharing ideas and best practices in strengthening the country's landscape sector.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Thai students left in disbelief after deadly school shooting
Article:
NONTHABURI, Thailand: Sobbing Thai students embraced each other tightly on Friday after a 14-year-old classmate entered their school wielding his grandfather's handgun and shot dead at least five school staff.
Tearful students in school uniforms held each other outside the Debsirin Nonthaburi secondary school while emergency workers treated injuries and parents looked for their children.
"I'm still in shock," 16-year-old Thatchai Jaiyen told AFP, expressing disbelief that a kind former teacher of his had been killed.
"She was such a good person. I thought that if she had encountered the shooter, she might have been able to reason with him.
"I never expected that the child would actually shoot her," he said, his voice trailing away.
The suspect first killed his grandparents at their home around 20km away with the same firearm, according to authorities.
He took his own life after killing a maths teacher, a Thai language teacher, a guidance counsellor, a student affairs administrator and a secretary at the school, according to police.
Debsirin Nonthaburi secondary is among the most prominent government schools in Nonthaburi province, just north of the capital Bangkok.
Grade 12 student Pakonkiat Sangchan was studying when he said he saw the shooter walking towards the building.
"My friend suggested that we start running, so that's what we did. We just ran," the 17-year-old said.
- 'CAN'T BELIEVE' -
Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul told reporters that the boy's dead grandmother "used to be a teacher and she was quite strict on him about studying."
Student Purin Khumchoo said he felt the suspect was "a troubled kid" but had appeared "very professional" when he had aimed the gun at him at school on Friday.
"My group of friends who knew him said he was interested in the FBI and guns, and that he was bullied by many other students," the 17-year-old said.
Purin said he felt depressed and bad for the people who were killed.
"The two teachers who were killed were lovely, and many students became better people because of them," he told AFP.
Pawarisa Maylissa, a grade 12 student, said she was in a computer lesson when her teacher told the class about the active shooting.
They shut the classroom door, locked themselves inside and hid between tables, just before Pawarisa heard multiple shots fired.
At the home of the shooter's grandparents, a neighbour said she heard two loud bangs early on Friday morning.
"I didn't know if it was firecrackers or gunshots," said the woman, who declined to give her name. "I was shocked."
She said the grandmother had taught her son. Another neighbour said she had been his teacher at primary and secondary school.
Thriwit Sukkasampraset, 18, said the shooter "liked playing basketball in front of his house and walking his dog."
Thailand has one of the highest rates of gun ownership in the region and past promises of tightening gun laws have not prevented repeated shootings.
"I can't believe how a child like him could get access to a gun," Pawarisa said.
"I'm a bit worried that other kids might also have guns," she said.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia, Singapore to strengthen labour cooperation, gig worker protection
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia and Singapore will continue to strengthen cooperation in the labour sector, including enhancing the welfare and protection of gig workers, as both countries navigate an increasingly dynamic employment landscape.
Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said the matter was among those discussed during his meeting with Singapore's acting Manpower Minister Jasmin Lau in conjunction with his official working visit to the republic today.
He said both sides exchanged views on current labour market developments and the challenges facing Malaysia and Singapore in preparing their workforce to meet the demands of the future economy.
"Malaysia and Singapore are facing rapid changes in the employment landscape. We therefore need to ensure that labour policies and worker protection continue to evolve in tandem with changing work arrangements and the needs of the economy," he said in a statement.
Ramanan said the discussions also covered talent development, upskilling initiatives and the need to prepare a workforce that is better equipped to adapt to technological advancements and artificial intelligence.
He said the sharing of experiences and best practices between the two countries was vital in building a progressive and inclusive employment ecosystem without compromising workers' interests and welfare.
He added that Malaysia and Singapore shared a unique and close labour relationship, creating greater opportunities for both countries to explore new areas of collaboration in talent and skills development.
"The relationship between Malaysia and Singapore extends beyond that of two neighbouring countries. Labour mobility, economic ties and people-to-people relations between our two nations are also very close.
"That is why we see significant opportunities to strengthen cooperation, share expertise and jointly address the workforce challenges that lie ahead," he said.
Also present at the meeting were Singapore Manpower Ministry Planning and Finance Programme Department director Pung Wan Qing, Employment Standards and Inclusive Workplaces director Gan Su Yi, SkillsFuture Singapore Agency (SSG) Corporate Planning Division director Kevin Lee, and Singapore Manpower Ministry Strategy and Ecosystem Development deputy director Lock Hong Quan.
Earlier, Ramanan visited Grab's headquarters in Singapore as part of his official working visit.

Title: 'Efforts to increase defence allocation reflects govt's commitment to modernise armed forces'
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's plan to increase the defence allocation under the 2027 Budget reflects the government's commitment to modernising the armed forces.
Armed Forces chief General Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman said the military appreciated the government's commitment to strengthening the forces' development, operational readiness and the welfare of its personnel and their families.
"This commitment demonstrates the government's determination to support efforts to develop and modernise the aarmed forces into a superior force and an integrated deterrent serving as the nation's primary line of defence," he told Bernama.
He said the additional allocation would support the modernisation of assets and equipment in line with its "Future Force" strategic development plan.
Malek said improving the welfare and quality of life of personnel would also boost morale and enable them to carry out their duties with greater commitment.
Earlier today, Anwar said at the
Semarak Kenegaraan
programme with the armed forces at Terendak Camp in Melaka that the government would seek to
increase the defence allocation
under next year's budget.
Anwar, who is also finance minister, said the increased allocation would also encompass personnel welfare, including efforts to improve housing quarters, construct a new hospital and maintain basic utilities such as water supply.
He also said the government has agreed in principle to
simplify and expedite
the promotion process for armed forces and police personnel, in line with other public service schemes.

Title: Bodies of three policemen killed in electrocution tragedy flown home [WATCH]
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: The bodies of three policemen electrocuted to death in Beaufort yesterday were flown to their respective hometowns tonight aboard Royal Malaysian Air Force and police aircraft.
Bernama observed the RMAF aircraft carrying the bodies of Corporal Mohamad Nur Hafiz Ibrahim and Constable Muhammad Raimi Ismarubee depart from Kota Kinabalu International Airport about 7.10pm.
The aircraft was scheduled to fly to the RMAF air base in Kuantan before continuing to the base in Gong Kedak, Terengganu.
The body of Corporal Chiu Teck Siong was taken to the police air wing base here before being flown to Sarawak aboard a police aircraft.
Earlier, all three bodies underwent post-mortem examinations at noon before being released from the Forensics Department of Queen Elizabeth Hospital at 2.56pm for repatriation to their respective hometowns.
Chiu, 40, from Sarawak, Mohamad Nur Hafiz, 29, from Kelantan and Muhammad Raimi, 26, from Terengganu, are believed to have been electrocuted in an incident outside the Weston police station in Beaufort about 5.50pm yesterday.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Home, Transport ministries given two weeks to submit airport security plan to cabinet
Article:
SANDAKAN: The cabinet has given the Home and Transport ministries two weeks to submit a comprehensive plan to strengthen airport security.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the move followed the cabinet's concern over recent incidents that had affected the country's image and created the impression that there are weaknesses in airport security.
"The cabinet takes a serious view of the incidents that have occurred, as they give the impression that security controls at our airports have been breached.
"Immediate steps are being taken to draft a detailed improvement plan involving various agencies," he told reporters after visiting several islands in the Eastern Sabah Security Zone (Ess Zone) with foreign diplomats.
Also present were Eastern Sabah Security Command (Esscom) commander Datuk Victor Sanjos and its chief executive officer Datuk Dr Jamaluddin Mohd Ali.
Attention has turned to airport security following several recent cases involving Malaysians, including the arrest of a Malaysian pilot after about 25kg of MDMA drugs was seized at Indonesia's Soekarno-Hatta Airport last week.
Meanwhile, Saifuddin said his ministry is also stepping up efforts to encourage diplomats and foreign representatives to review and relax travel advisories for the east coast of Sabah, following the improved security situation in the area.
"Several foreign countries, including Japan and Switzerland, have already amended their travel advisories as a result of continuous briefings and proof of stability in the local security environment," he said.
The initiative was reinforced through a security familiarisation visit involving 14 diplomatic representatives, who visited strategic locations and key tourist destinations.
"This programme brings foreign representatives to visit the ESS Zone to see for themselves the state of peace and tourism potential, thereby enabling them to convey accurate, factual and balanced information to their respective countries," he said.
Commenting on security controls in the area, he said between January and June 30, Esscom conducted 897,293 inspections and made 307 arrests.
He added that enforcement operations over the six-month period also recorded 38 seizures valued at RM23.37 million through tight controls on land and in state waters.
To ensure national sovereignty continues to be safeguarded, Saifuddin said the federal government has allocated a total of RM723 million to the Ess Zone over Esscom's 13 years of operation for asset procurement, operations and logistics.

Title: Bank Negara governor: Malaysia remains resilient in facing global crises
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia successfully weathered various global crises, including the Asian financial crisis, the Covid-19 pandemic and conflicts in the Middle East while maintaining the resilience of the country's economic fundamentals
Bank Negara Malaysia Governor Datuk Seri Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour said the achievement was supported by four key buffers, namely economic and trading partner diversification, clear economic policies, sufficient fiscal space, and strong international reserves.
"These are strong economic fundamentals that are important for us to maintain at all times so that whatever happens in other countries, we are able to withstand it, navigate through it with confidence, and ensure it does not affect the growth of our national economy," he told Buletin TV3 at BNM headquarters.
He said the experience of facing several previous crises has taught Malaysia not to depend on any particular economic sector or trading partner.
"We do not depend on a single market alone. No single trading partner accounts for more than 16 per cent of our total exports," he said.
Rasheed said clear policies continue to support the country's economic fundamentals despite facing uncertainties, while sufficient fiscal space enables the government to address economic shocks.
"In terms of policies related to targeted fuel subsidies and so on, they have created fiscal space for the government to cover expenses in the event of a crisis," he said.
He said the country's international reserves have also remained strong, increasing to US132 billion compared with US113 billion in 2023.
Despite the positive economic performance, Rasheed advised the public to continue spending prudently in order to prepare for any uncertainties or emergencies.

Title: MACC completes 4-day interview in RM370mil share purchase probe
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) today completed a four-day interview with a former chief financial officer of a company owned by a statutory body as part of investigations into alleged abuse of power involving the purchase of shares in two plantation companies worth about RM370 million.
MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said today marked the fourth and final day of questioning the former senior officer, who was first called in on Tuesday.
"Today's recording session began at 9am and ended at 6.30pm.
"Today was the final day for the MACC to record the former senior officer's statement," he said.
The investigation focuses on alleged abuse of power in connection with the acquisition of shares in the two plantation companies.
