Title: Stay or go? DAP faces catch-22 as crucial congress vote looms
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 8 — DAP delegates will gather on August 16 for the party’s national congress, where they will face a political catch-22 that could shape its strategy heading into the next general election.
Roughly 4,000 delegates are expected to vote on whether DAP leaders should remain in government posts, including the federal Cabinet, or relinquish those positions while continuing to support Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim in Parliament.
The decision comes after a difficult 10 months for the party.
DAP lost all eight seats it contested in the Sabah election last November before suffering further setbacks in Johor and Negeri Sembilan.
Among the casualties was its secretary-general Anthony Loke Siew Fook, who lost his Chennah state seat in the Jelebu parliamentary constituency after serving three terms.
The Cabinet dilemma
The setbacks have fuelled frustration among grassroots members who believe governing has cost DAP politically without producing enough reforms to justify the compromises made over the past three and a half years.
Delegates are now weighing two competing risks.
Grassroots frustration has grown over what members see as insufficient reform despite DAP’s compromises during more than three years in government. — File picture by Shafwan Zaidon
Remaining in government could reinforce criticism that the party has compromised too much while reforms have progressed too slowly.
Leaving the Cabinet, meanwhile, could satisfy members demanding a stronger stance but create a different political challenge.
Many voters may not distinguish between leaving the executive and continuing to support the government in Parliament.
Instead, a Cabinet exit could be viewed as a sign that the unity government is losing cohesion before the next general election, which must be held by February 2028.
The competing pressures reflect the different audiences DAP is trying to address.
Grassroots members want the party to acknowledge that recent election setbacks were linked to slower-than-expected reforms while in government.
Many voters, meanwhile, may expect parties in government to complete a full parliamentary term, particularly after stability has been repeatedly presented as essential for economic growth and policy reforms.
A precedent in Melaka
DAP leaders have already ruled out withdrawing parliamentary support for Anwar or leaving Pakatan Harapan.
The proposed arrangement of relinquishing executive positions while remaining politically aligned with the government has a recent, though not exact, parallel in Melaka.
Last month, Melaka DAP withdrew from the state government after objecting to a Bill allowing the appointment of nominated assemblymen.
Its representatives resigned from their state administration posts and its four assemblymen moved to the Opposition bench, although the BN-led state government remained intact as BN retained a two-thirds majority in the assembly.
The August 16 vote will determine whether DAP adopts a similar arrangement at the federal level by remaining part of the governing coalition while stepping out of the executive.
No easy answer
International Islamic University Malaysia political scientist Associate Professor Syaza Shukri said the debate ultimately centres on whether voters believe the government’s reform agenda has delivered meaningful change.
“The biggest concern is the lack of reform and when we say reform we have to understand it’s about reforms that are felt on the ground.
“Meaning that economic reforms that improve lives and ease of doing business. We’re talking about reforms that would not make Malaysians feel marginalised. Things seem to stay the same,” she said.
Syaza said a vote to remain in government would suggest delegates had chosen the more pragmatic course of helping the administration continue implementing its agenda.
Recent tensions between DAP and Umno surfaced in Negeri Sembilan after Ahmad Zahid Hamidi urged voters to ‘kasi bungkus’ Anthony Loke, highlighting strains between key partners in the unity government. — File picture by Yusof Mat Isa
“But the implication is how can they explain this to the grassroots. Because pragmatism is basically the compromise thus far and we know that’s not very popular.”
She described leaving the Cabinet while maintaining parliamentary support as the clearest middle ground.
“I think this is already the best middle ground, which is leaving the Cabinet but not pulling parliamentary support.
“Pulling parliamentary support would cause the fall of the government. Not doing anything would not solve anything as well,” she said.
Even so, Syaza believes many Malaysians may not appreciate the distinction.
“Average voters may not understand the difference between pulling out of executive versus legislative. So public perception would be that Anwar has lost confidence.”
She said such a perception could weaken Pakatan Harapan heading into the next general election, particularly as Barisan Nasional and Perikatan Nasional appear to have regained political momentum.
Akademi Nusantara senior fellow Azmi Hassan also expects delegates to favour leaving the Cabinet while maintaining support for Anwar.
He said delegates broadly reflect the mood among grassroots members and supporters.
“I think they are more effective as the critical voice of the government. Similar to Umno, they have their Pemuda, which should be very critical of the top leadership. So DAP should be there. I think they are good at that,” he said.
According to Azmi, remaining in government has limited DAP’s ability to champion policies that resonate with its supporters.
“So I think it is best for them to opt out of the government but at the same time support the prime minister so that the stability of the Anwar government remains intact,” he said.
He said the congress provides delegates with an opportunity to reassess the party’s direction after successive election setbacks while keeping Pakatan Harapan intact ahead of GE16.
Leaving the Cabinet could give DAP greater distance from the government, but voters may interpret the move as a sign that Anwar has lost confidence within his coalition. — Bernama file pic
Looking ahead to GE16
Whichever way delegates vote, the political risks remain.
Remaining in government could deepen frustration among members who believe the party needs greater distance from the administration.
Leaving the Cabinet could satisfy those members while inviting questions over the unity government’s cohesion and DAP’s ability to influence policy from outside the executive.
The result is expected to shape DAP’s role in government for the remainder of the parliamentary term, as well as how the party positions itself before Malaysians return to the general polls.

Title: Anwar: Govt to cut red tape in military, police promotion process
Article:
MELAKA, Aug 7 — The government has, in principle, agreed to reduce bureaucratic hurdles and expedite the promotion process for personnel of the Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) and the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM), bringing it in line with the promotion system for the rest of the public service.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said details of the new mechanism are expected to be announced during the Ambang Merdeka celebration at Stadium Merdeka in Kuala Lumpur on August 30.
He said Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar and Public Service director-general Tan Sri Wan Ahmad Dahlan Abdul Aziz are currently finalising the implementation mechanism.
“We will give them a little more time,” he said when addressing the ‘Semarak Kenegaraan’ programme with MAF personnel at Terendak Camp here today.
Also present were Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Datuk Dr Mohd Na’im Mokhtar, Deputy Defence Minister Adly Zahari, Shamsul Azri and Army Chief Gen Tan Sri Azhan Md Othman.
Anwar said the issue of promotions for MAF officers was raised directly with him during his visit to Syed Sirajuddin Camp in Gemas, Negeri Sembilan, last month. — Bernama

Title: Anwar questions RM330m gap in proposed Felda hotel sale, orders full report
Article:
MELAKA, Aug 7 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has directed the management of the Federal Land Development Authority (Felda) to provide a complete report regarding the proposed sale of a hotel owned by the agency, which was allegedly at a price far lower than the original purchase price.
Anwar, who is also the Finance Minister, revealed that he refused to sign the approval document for the sale after discovering that the hotel was to be sold for £100 million (RM550 million), whereas it had been purchased by the previous management for £160 million (RM880 million).
He also expressed his regret over the loss-making sale proposal, considering that Felda settlers are still facing various hardships and require government assistance to improve basic facilities.
“Felda is under my watch. Two months ago, the Felda management came and asked me to sign for the sale of this hotel. I said, wait a moment, what kind of business is this? Selling at a price lower than when it was bought. So I did not sign. I said, find out who did this and submit a report.
“Felda settlers are struggling. When I visited (the settlers), they said they wanted air conditioning, schools to be repaired, and their income is insufficient. But Felda itself (the loss-making sale) is just casually losing money,” he said in his speech at the “Semarak Kenegaraan Programme” with the Malaysian Armed Forces at Terendak Camp here today.
Also present at the event were Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan, Deputy Defence Minister Adly Zahari, Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar and Army Chief Gen Tan Sri Azhan Md Othman.
According to the Prime Minister, the move to request Felda to submit a complete report is to defend Felda as an important institution in Malaysia.
“If we don’t (do something), no matter how long, our agencies — including Malay agencies that we take pride in and want to defend — this is what will become of them. So we must correct that,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia and Singapore to deepen labour cooperation, boost protection for gig workers
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 7 — Malaysia and Singapore will continue to strengthen cooperation in the labour sector, including enhancing the welfare and protection of gig workers, as both countries navigate an increasingly dynamic employment landscape.
Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said the matter was among those discussed during his meeting with Singapore’s Acting Minister for Manpower Jasmin Lau in conjunction with his official working visit to the republic today.
He said both sides exchanged views on current labour market developments and the challenges facing Malaysia and Singapore in preparing their workforce to meet the demands of the future economy.
“Malaysia and Singapore are facing rapid changes in the employment landscape. We therefore need to ensure that labour policies and worker protection continue to evolve in tandem with changing work arrangements and the needs of the economy,” he said in a statement today.
Ramanan said the discussions also covered talent development, upskilling initiatives and the need to prepare a workforce that is better equipped to adapt to technological advancements and artificial intelligence (AI).
He said the sharing of experiences and best practices between the two countries was vital in building a progressive and inclusive employment ecosystem without compromising workers’ interests and welfare.
Ramanan said Malaysia and Singapore shared a unique and close labour relationship, creating greater opportunities for both countries to explore new areas of collaboration in talent and skills development.
“The relationship between Malaysia and Singapore extends beyond that of two neighbouring countries. Labour mobility, economic ties and people-to-people relations between our two nations are also very close.
“That is why we see significant opportunities to strengthen cooperation, share expertise and jointly address the workforce challenges that lie ahead,” he said.
Also present at the meeting were Singapore Ministry of Manpower Planning and Finance Programme Department director Pung Wan Qing, Employment Standards and Inclusive Workplaces director Gan Su Yi, SkillsFuture Singapore Agency (SSG) Corporate Planning Division director Kevin Lee, and Singapore Ministry of Manpower Strategy and Ecosystem Development deputy director Lock Hong Quan.
Earlier, Ramanan visited Grab’s headquarters in Singapore as part of his official working visit. — Bernama

Title: Woman hurt after SUV crashes into KKIA departure hall
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Aug 7 — A woman was injured after the sport utility vehicle (SUV) she was driving reportedly lost control and crashed through the glass entrance of the departure hall at Kota Kinabalu International Airport (KKIA) this afternoon.
The incident, which occurred at about 4.20pm, shattered the glass doors of the departure hall and sent broken glass across the passenger walkway, causing panic among members of the public at the scene.
Early indications suggest the driver may have accidentally pressed the accelerator, causing the vehicle to surge forward and crash into the terminal.
However, no passengers or airport staff were injured in the incident.
The driver sustained injuries and was taken to hospital for treatment.
Several videos circulating on social media showed a white SUV with severe damage to its front after crashing into the terminal entrance, with shattered glass scattered across the area.
Kota Kinabalu police chief Assistant Commissioner Shahrudin Mat Husain said investigations are underway to determine the exact cause of the crash.

Title: Ismail Sabri stable after successful pacemaker implantation at IJN
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 7 — Former prime minister Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob’s pacemaker implantation procedure this afternoon at the National Heart Institute (IJN) was carried out successfully, his lawyer has confirmed.
When contacted by
Malay Mail
, Ismail Sabri’s lawyer Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad confirmed that “the procedure went smoothly and was successful”.
“Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri is stable but remains in the CCU for close monitoring,” he said, referring to IJN’s Coronary Care Unit by its initials.
IJN later said Ismail Sabri had successfully undergone a leadless pacemaker implantation procedure for an abnormal heart rhythm this afternoon.
The institute said he had been advised to rest following the procedure, with visits limited to close family members to support his recovery and ensure his privacy.
IJN also asked the media and public to respect the privacy of Ismail Sabri and his family during this period, adding that further updates would be issued through authorised channels where appropriate.
Ismail Sabri was initially expected to be charged at the Sessions Court in Kuala Lumpur today under the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Act, reportedly in relation to asset declaration.
But this morning, the Sessions Court decided to allow Ismail Sabri’s request, made through his lawyers, to postpone the reading of the charge against him to August 27 due to health reasons, as the prosecution did not object.
Amer Hamzah had informed the court that Ismail Sabri had been admitted to IJN and warded there since yesterday, after Ismail Sabri experienced health issues while having his statement recorded at the MACC headquarters.
Amer Hamzah said that the doctor in charge had confirmed that Ismail Sabri had “possible arrhythmia that requires further investigation.”
The lawyer had also said that Ismail Sabri would undergo a pacemaker procedure this afternoon and would need to remain warded after the procedure, before proposing the August 27 date.
In court, the prosecution cited “humanitarian grounds” when it did not object to the application to postpone the case to August 27, as Ismail Sabri could not appear in court due to his health condition and as he is under MACC bail.
Bera MP Ismail Sabri, 66, is a former Umno vice-president and was Malaysia’s ninth prime minister from August 2021 to October 2022.

Title: Malaysia to increase defence spending in Budget 2027, says Anwar
Article:
MELAKA, Aug 7 — The government will seek to increase defence allocation in Budget 2027 to strengthen the Malaysian Armed Forces’ (MAF) readiness and improve personnel welfare, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said greater investment was necessary to safeguard national peace, which he described as the country’s most valuable asset.
“Defence readiness must be maintained at all times because conflicts do not occur when expected. We cannot wait for another country to declare war before we begin preparing,” he said at the Semarak Kenegaraan programme with the MAF at Terendak Camp here today.
Anwar also called for military weapons and equipment to be procured systematically and transparently, without profiteering or excessive commissions paid to outside agents.
Also present were Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Senator Dr Zulkifli Hasan, Deputy Defence Minister Adly Zahari, Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar and Army chief General Tan Sri Azhan Md Othman.
Anwar said the proposed increase would cover personnel welfare, including upgraded living quarters, a new hospital and maintenance of basic facilities such as water supplies.
“Over the past three years, the Madani Government has increased the Defence Ministry’s allocation by more than 35 per cent.
“This is not a small increase, but it is not widely known. Expressions of support and concern mean little if equipment remains in poor condition or procurement is mired in controversy,” he said.
Anwar said the improving economy would allow the government to consider higher defence allocation, supported by a stronger ringgit, increased foreign investment and controlled inflation.
Budget 2027 is scheduled to be tabled in the Dewan Rakyat on October 9.
At the event, Anwar also announced RM147,000 for the Armed Forces Family Welfare Association and RM1 million to maintain mosques and prayer halls at four military camps in Melaka: Terendak, Sungai Udang, Masjid Tanah and Bukit Beruang. — Bernama

Title: MACC urges ministry chiefs to protect whistleblowers as Malaysia eyes higher CPI ranking
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 7 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has called on ministry secretaries-general and department directors-general to prioritise whistleblower protection to strengthen governance and elevate Malaysia’s position in the Corruption Perceptions Index (CPI) by 2030.
MACC’s National Governance Planning Division deputy director Mohd Gunawan Che Ab Aziz said the move is critical to remove civil servants’ fear of reporting misconduct and, in turn, bolster organisational integrity.
He said secretaries-general and directors-general must translate the government’s commitment to amending the Whistleblower Protection Act 2010 down to the grassroots level, to ensure that the Integrity Unit in every ministry functions independently and reports directly to the MACC.
“The Organisational Anti-Corruption Plan (OACP) must also serve as a key performance indicator (KPI) for promotions of high-ranking officers, to ensure the anti-corruption agenda is carried out effectively,” he said in a commentary piece titled “Upholding the CPI Mandate: Radical Reform Now in the Hands of Secretaries-General and Directors-General.”
Mohd Gunawan said that beyond strengthening whistleblower protection, secretaries-general and directors-general must lead comprehensive reforms in public procurement and contract systems, including full open tenders and mandatory declarations of beneficial ownership for all bidding companies.
He said the move is in line with the National Anti-Corruption Strategy (NACS) 2024-2028 to curb cronyism and proxy practices. He also hopes the Government Procurement Act will be expedited to provide a stronger legal framework.
He further proposed fully digitalising government service delivery to reduce discretion and physical interactions that could lead to corruption.
He said AI systems, algorithm-driven automatic approvals, and digital audit trails would enhance transparency and allow irregularities to be detected in real-time.
“Moreover, every ministry must adopt stricter accountability concerning reprimands in the Auditor-General’s Report, including setting a maximum three-month period to execute corrective or disciplinary action for weaknesses raised.
“This approach must be supported by open data policies to allow ministerial expenditure to be scrutinised transparently by the media and public,” he said.
Mohd Gunawan stressed that Malaysia should not be complacent with its current achievement, despite rising to 54th place out of 182 countries in the 2025 CPI with a score of 52 points.
He said the target of reaching the top 25 by 2030 requires a more aggressive and structured shift, with secretaries-general and directors-general leading the way as champions of integrity in the public service. — Bernama

Title: Yayasan Tuanku Fauziah launches Women in Technology Awards 2026 to honour Malaysian innovators
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Aug 7 — Yayasan Tuanku Fauziah (YTF) has launched the Women in Technology Awards 2026, a national initiative to recognise outstanding Malaysian women, whose leadership, innovation and technological achievements are shaping the country’s future.
The awards, organised with the Malaysian Industry Government Group for High Technology (MIGHT) as technical partner open for nominations from August 10 to September 5. Both self-nominations and third-party submissions from industry, academia, government, startups and research institutions are welcomed.
Two categories will be offered — the Senior Women in Technology Award, worth RM30,000, for professionals with at least 20 years’ experience, and the Junior Women in Technology Award, worth RM15,000, for innovators aged 35 and below or with under 10 years’ experience.
YTF said the awards celebrate exceptional Malaysian women whose contributions have advanced science, technology and innovation, inspiring greater participation in STEM and encouraging future generations of innovators and leaders.
Award recipients will be honoured at the YTF Gala Dinner on October 17, with nominations evaluated on professional achievements, innovation, national impact and contributions to Malaysia’s technology ecosystem.
Interested individuals and organisations may submit nominations through the official portal at
https://might.org.my/women-in-technology-awards/
.
For further enquiries on the awards and nomination process, contact YTF Women in Technology Award 2026 consultant Sheriffah Noor Khamseah Al-Idid at sheriffahkhamseah@gmail.com or MIGHT Head of Smart & Sustainable Cities Anusha Magendram at anusha@might.org.my.

Title: Immigration Dept gears up for F1 Bahrain GP visitor surge at Sepang
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 7 — The Immigration Department (JIM) will ensure that immigration procedures involving visas and related passes at the country’s entry points run smoothly during the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) this October.
Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said the department would work closely with the Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) to ensure clearance procedures at the country's entry points are carried out efficiently while complying with all security requirements.
“We must provide the best possible service to ensure the smooth organisation of the Formula 1 event.
“For entry point operations, we will work with AKPS to ensure clearance procedures are carried out smoothly. The role involves matters relating to visas and passes,” he said at the department’s monthly assembly here today.
Drawing on Malaysia's experience as a former Formula 1 host, Zakaria said previous races attracted more than 100,000 spectators, while organisers are targeting about 150,000 visitors for this year’s event.
He said the number of foreign visitors could reach 300,000, based on attendance recorded at several Formula 1 races in countries such as France and Japan.
“This event could attract as many as 300,000 foreign tourists and visitors. Therefore, immigration procedures must be efficient and swift to ensure everything proceeds smoothly,” he said.
Zakaria said JIM had proposed several measures to facilitate the event, including arrangements involving the Malaysian Digital Arrival Card (MDAC) for race crews, drivers and other related personnel, subject to government approval.
Formula 1 and the Fédération Internationale de l’Automobile (FIA) previously announced that the 2026 Bahrain Grand Prix would be held at SIC from October 2 to 4 as part of a collaboration between Malaysia and Bahrain.
The Bahrain Grand Prix was originally scheduled to be held at the Bahrain International Circuit in April before being postponed to October due to geopolitical tensions in West Asia.
SIC hosted the Malaysian Grand Prix from 1999 to 2017 before the race was dropped from the Formula 1 calendar due to rising hosting costs and licensing fees. — Bernama

Title: Immigration busts ‘flying passport’ syndicate, three arrested in Johor
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 7 — The Immigration Department of Malaysia (JIM) has dismantled a “flying passport” syndicate with the arrest of three suspects at the Sultan Abu Bakar Complex (KSAB) in Gelang Patah, Johor, yesterday, said Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban.
He said the operation, which began at 10am, involved a team of officers and personnel from the Putrajaya Immigration headquarters Intelligence and Special Operations Division and Johor JIM.
“This success was the result of follow-up action by JIM based on developments from investigations under Ops Crack conducted earlier in collaboration with the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC).
“The operations team was deployed to the location and detained three individuals aged between 33 and 41,” he said in a statement today.
He said the team also seized mobile phones, keys to a premise, jewellery, Immigration security stamps and RM20,000 in cash.
According to Zakaria, the suspects were detained for allegedly committing offences under Section 12(1)(h) of the Passport Act 1966 and were taken to the Immigration Office for further action.
He said the syndicate’s modus operandi involved collecting passports belonging to foreign nationals without requiring the document owners’ physical presence at the country’s entry points.
“Copies of the passport front pages were then sent by the syndicate’s agents via WhatsApp to collaborators to be scanned, creating false movement records in JIM’s system,” he said, adding that agents charged RM700 for each foreign passport using the syndicate’s services.
Zakaria stressed that investigations would continue to identify the syndicate’s network.
“Firm action will be taken to curb any activities that violate the law to ensure the country’s stability and prosperity continue to be safeguarded,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Indonesian maid jailed four years for neglect that led to toddler’s drowning in Sentul pool
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 7 — An Indonesian domestic helper was sentenced to four years’ jail by the Sessions Court here today after she pleaded guilty to neglecting a boy, resulting in his death by drowning in an adult swimming pool last month.
Judge Suhaila Haron imposed the jail sentence on Wahyuni Tanjung, 44, and ordered it to run from the date of her arrest on July 29.
According to the charge, Wahyuni, as a person responsible for the care of a two-year-three-month-old boy, neglected the child, resulting in his death.
She was charged with committing the offence at the adult swimming pool of a residential complex in Sentul between 6pm and 7pm on July 28, under Section 31(1)(a) of the Child Act 2001, which provides for a maximum fine of RM50,000, imprisonment of up to 20 years, or both upon conviction.
According to the facts of the case, the victim’s mother had instructed the accused, who was employed as her domestic helper, to take the victim and his five-year-old brother to the swimming pool at their residential complex on the day of the incident.
At about 7pm, the accused contacted the victim’s mother to inform her that the child had drowned, after which a member of the public performed cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) on him.
The victim was subsequently taken to Selayang Hospital and admitted to the Intensive Care Unit (ICU), where he was pronounced dead at 4am the following day.
An autopsy conducted by the Kuala Lumpur Hospital Forensic Department found that the cause of death was consistent with drowning.
Investigations found that the accused, who had worked for only a month, had taken the victim and his brother to an adult swimming pool without any swimming aids despite knowing that both children could not swim, and left them unattended when she went to the toilet.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Md Subri Hashim urged the court to impose a sentence that would serve as a lesson to the accused and other child caregivers.
“The accused, as a person employed by the victim’s mother to work and assist in caring for the children, should not have left the victim and his brother without proper supervision.
“The court should take into account the seriousness of the offence, which resulted in the death of the victim, who should have had the opportunity to live a longer life,” he said.
Wahyuni, who was unrepresented, appeared emotional when shown photographs from the victim’s autopsy report.
The accused did not appeal for a lighter sentence but told the court that her husband had died 14 years ago and that she had a 16-year-old son in Indonesia. — Bernama

Title: Remains of three policemen killed in Beaufort electrocution incident sent home after post-mortem
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Aug 7 — The remains of three police officers who died believed to be from electrocution outside the Weston Police Station, Beaufort, yesterday afternoon were brought out from the Forensic Department of the Queen Elizabeth Hospital (HQE) at 2:55 pm today to be sent back to their respective hometowns.
The post-mortem process, which began at 8.30am, concluded at 12pm before proceeding with documentation procedures to allow all the remains to be transported to their respective destinations.
The remains of Corporal Chiu Teck Siong will be taken to the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) Air Operations Force (PGU) Airfield here before being flown to Sarawak.
Meanwhile, the remains of the other two officers, Corporal Mohamad Nur Hafiz Ibrahim and Constable Muhammad Raimi Ismarubee, will be taken to the Sabah Contingent Police Headquarters (IPK) Mosque here to have the funeral prayers performed after Maghrib.
Following the prayers, their remains will be sent to the Kota Kinabalu International Airport (KKIA) before being flown to Kelantan and Terengganu using a Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) aircraft.
Meanwhile, Beaufort District Police Chief Supt Champin Piuh expressed his appreciation to Sabah Police Commissioner Datuk Jauteh Dikun, members of the Sabah Contingent Police Headquarters (IPK), and HQE for their extensive assistance in facilitating the management of the remains.
He also recorded his appreciation to the leaders of the Klias and Lumadan constituencies, Datuk Isnin Aliasnih and Datuk Ruslan Muharam, as well as the Sabah Contingent Junior Police Officers Association for the support and cooperation provided throughout the management process.
“Sincere contributions from the Sabah PDRM personnel were also handed over to the families of the three officers as a token of solidarity and appreciation for their sacrifices,” he told reporters when met at the hospital.
In the incident at 5.50pm yesterday, the three officers stationed at the Weston Police Station were confirmed dead after they were believed to have been electrocuted while harvesting coconuts using an iron pole near the police station. — Bernama

Title: Bersatu sec‑gen Azmin Ali says party remains legitimate Perikatan component despite PAS claim
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Aug 7 — Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu) secretary-general Datuk Seri Mohamed Azmin Ali today hit back at PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang’s assertion that the party’s membership in Perikatan Nasional (PN) had automatically lapsed, describing the claim as unconstitutional.
In a statement, Azmin said no clause in the PN constitution allowed a member party’s membership to lapse on its own. He stressed that Bersatu’s position could only be decided by the PN presidential council under Clause 7A of the coalition’s constitution.
“To date, the presidential council has never met to determine Bersatu’s membership. Therefore, Bersatu remains a legitimate component party of Perikatan Nasional,” Azmin said.
He added that the PAS president had no veto power to decide Bersatu’s status, and his remarks reflected a lack of understanding of the coalition’s constitution.
Under Clause 7 of the PN constitution, each member party has full rights to attend, express views and vote in meetings of the supreme council, state liaison bodies and area liaison bodies.
Azmin also accused the coalition’s leadership of breaching its constitution by barring Bersatu representatives from attending the PN supreme council meeting on July 16, which decided seat allocations and cooperation with Barisan Nasional for the recent Negeri Sembilan state election.
He said Bersatu would lodge a formal complaint with the Registrar of Societies over what it described as a serious violation of the coalition’s constitution, adding that Perikatan, now dominated by PAS, had disregarded good governance principles and acted recklessly and undemocratically.

Title: Border agency seizes falsely declared frozen chicken, pork worth RM3.42m at Sepanggar Port
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Aug 7 — The Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) has seized 12 containers carrying frozen animal products worth an estimated RM3.42 million at Sepanggar Port.
The seizure was the result of an enforcement operation targeting false import declarations.
AKPS director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain said the seizure involved 348,000kg of frozen chicken and pork believed to have been brought into the country through declarations that did not match the cargo.
He said the integrated operation, dubbed Ops Ribat Sepanggar 1/2026, began on May 19 with the cooperation of the Royal Malaysian Customs Department, Sabah State Health Department, Department of Veterinary Services Sabah, and the port authority.
“The 12 containers were identified before being inspected at Sepanggar Port on July 16. They contained frozen chicken and pork believed to have been imported using inconsistent declarations,” he told a press conference at Sepanggar Port here today.
According to him, the seized products are believed to have originated from China and Hong Kong.
The goods were confiscated for investigation under Section 133(1)(a) of the Customs Act 1967 for allegedly failing to make a full and accurate declaration and for submitting false or materially inaccurate documents.
“If convicted, offenders face a fine of up to RM500,000, imprisonment of up to five years, or both,” he said.
Mohd Shuhaily said AKPS viewed seriously any attempt to smuggle goods into the country through false declarations or breaches of import regulations, adding that the agency would continue strengthening inspections at the nation’s entry points through joint enforcement operations with relevant agencies. — The Borneo Post

Title: Anwar says GLICs deployed RM20.3b in domestic investments under GEAR-uP
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 7 — The Government-Linked Enterprises Activation and Reform Programme (GEAR-uP), which is entering its third year, saw government-linked investment companies (GLICs) allocating and deploying RM 20.3 billion domestically.
This was roughly three times the RM 6.6 billion allocated and deployed in 2024, with momentum carrying into the first quarter of 2026.
“This (GEAR-uP) is not capital seeking passive returns. It is national wealth mobilised with national purpose. We are only entering the third year of this journey. Much has been achieved, but much remains to be done,” Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said in the GEAR-uP Progress Report released today.
Spearheaded by the Ministry of Finance (MoF), GEAR-uP was launched in 2024 to unlock RM120 billion over five years, driving socioeconomic reforms and accelerating Malaysia’s industrial transformation.
The programme is anchored by six major GLICs: Khazanah Nasional Bhd (Khazanah), the Employees Provident Fund (EPF), Permodalan Nasional Bhd (PNB), Kumpulan Wang Persaraan (Diperbadankan) (KWAP), Lembaga Tabung Angkatan Tentera (LTAT), and Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH).
He said with this programme, Malaysia has chosen to invest in stability, strengthen resilience, and ensure that the gains of growth are felt where they matter most in the lives of ordinary Malaysians, amid an external environment that continues to shift due to global volatility.
“The work continues, and the rakyat remains our measure of success. If we stay the course, Insya-Allah, Malaysia can build a future worthy of its people,” said Anwar, who is also the finance minister.
Work in progress
The work continues with, among others, KWAP-backed Google’s Selangor data centre, which adds a further 320 MW and 26,500 jobs through 2026 and 2027, alongside Empyrion Digital’s phased build-out in Johor.
On firms and capital markets, GLIC funds such as Dana Impak, Dana Perintis, Dana Pemacu and Ekuinas, carry more companies from venture to growth stage, and Khazanah’s planned Dana Ciptawan adds a further RM200 million for Bumiputera enterprises and other mid-tier Malaysian firms, the report said.
Government-linked companies (GLCs) remain on course for RM 100 billion in additional market value by 2028, with MY Value Up now extending the same discipline to Malaysia’s 88 largest listed companies.
The Capital Market Masterplan’s target of RM5.8-RM6.3 trillion in market capitalisation by 2030 depends on this pipeline holding, it said.
Among others, Tenaga Nasional Bhd’s (TNB) grid investment continues under Regulatory Period 4, rising from RM 12 billion in 2025 towards RM 15 billion in 2027, as the country works towards 70 per cent renewable energy in installed capacity by 2050.
Malaysia Airports continues its five-year, RM11 billion upgrade programme, with Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA)’s capacity plan targeting over 100 million passengers.
On Bumiputera wealth and welfare, the report said ten companies are targeted for listing over 2026-2027. Concurrently, the 10 Bumiputera Champions Programme is supporting that effort by working to scale Bumiputera companies.
Zakat Wakalah is targeted to reach RM100 million in 2026, up from RM28 million the year before.
Fair pay, growth
Minister of Finance II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said GEAR-uP exists to ensure that the capital Malaysia commands does not merely pass through, but builds, settles and keeps growing.
“In 2025, this capital was allocated and deployed at roughly three times the level of the year before, and our portfolio of companies delivered a total shareholder return of 8.0 per cent.
“In time, the numbers will speak for themselves. What matters more is what those numbers translate into. Capital builds nothing on its own; an investment becomes prosperous only when a Malaysian is ready to fill the work it creates, and is paid fairly for it,” he added.
He said the GEAR-uP programme is measured not only in ringgit deployed, but in living wages adopted, in graduates placed in good jobs, in Bumiputera firms grown to scale, and in supply chains that take root on Malaysian soil.
The report, released by MoF, said although the external environment continues to shift through global volatility and reshaping of economies and trade, the Madani Economy remains the true north: an economy that raises its ceiling and its floor together.
“Malaysia was able to hold steady through external turbulence, as a result of earlier reforms in 2023.
“The direction for GEAR-uP was settled at the outset, in 2024. Everything since has been about delivery,” the report said, adding that the next three years carry real things to look forward to as most of them are already in motion and coming within reach of more Malaysians.
The report said the task of GEAR-uP has always been to turn the capital Malaysia attracts into enduring capability - an ecosystem deep enough to hold investment, firms that grow into champions, and capital that reaches the rakyat as better wages, stronger local supply chains and higher-value work.
It said true economic success is defined by what that capital builds and how widely it is felt.
“GLICs and GLCs mean to stay the course, to keep deploying, to keep delivering, and to let what is being built take roots and flourish,” the report concluded. — Bernama

Title: Anwar says constituency funds belong to people, not exclusive right of elected MPs
Article:
ALOR GAJAH, Aug 7 — Government funding allocated to a parliamentary constituency is intended for its constituents and is not the exclusive right of its elected Member of Parliament (MP), Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
He said the funds were meant to finance facilities and improvements that raised the living standards of the people in the constituency.
“Allocations do not necessarily have to be given to MPs. They are for the people.
“If RM2 million is allocated, it should go towards schools, religious schools, mosques, drain repairs and other local needs. We will ensure that happens,” he told reporters after performing Friday prayers at Masjid Ar-Rasyidin here today.
Also present were Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Senator Dr Zulkifli Hasan and Melaka Police chief Datuk Dzulkhairi Mukhtar.
Anwar said the policy had long been in place and was known to MPs who had previously served in government.
“If an MP is now in opposition, we will channel the funds directly to the people,” he said, in response to claims by several MPs that the government had withheld constituency funding from them.
Separately, Anwar said PKR deputy president Nurul Izzah, who is also his daughter, had other commitments requiring her attention temporarily, following her request to step down from her position yesterday.
“She has a special programme elsewhere for a while, so I said that was fine and we could accept it. But she remains active in the party,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Government prioritises new theatres to support surgeries during Sultanah Aminah Hospital upgrades
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Aug 7 — The Economy Ministry will prioritise building three to four new operating theatres at the Sultanah Aminah Hospital (HSA) while the mechanical and electrical (M&E) upgrades take place.
Its minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said the new operating theatres will complement the hospital’s existing 12 operating theatres that will also undergo part of the M&E upgrades.
“At present, HSA is undergoing the M&E upgrades and the initial plan was to temporarily move the existing operating theatres in phases by partial shutdowns.
“However, it was not possible due to technical issues and risks as the operating theatres cannot be partly closed or be temporarily moved.
“The only way is to build totally new operating theatres before replacing the old facilities in order to support the entire hospital’s M&E upgrades,” he said after a working visit to HSA here today.
Present during the working visit were Johor health director Dr Mohtar Pungut @ Ahmad and HSA director Dr Mohamad Nizam Subahir.
Akmal Nasrullah said the government will prioritise the building of the operating theatres to support ongoing surgeries and make way for the hospital’s upgrades.
“The construction of the new operating theatres will depend on the relevant agencies as there are several procedures involved.
“The ongoing M&E upgrades are part of seven upgrading projects worth RM1.139 billion that is currently being carried out at the hospital.
“The upgrades also involve the construction of an ambulatory care centre (ACC) for outpatient services which includes a multi-storey car park,” he said.
Akmal Nasrullah, who is also the Johor Bahru MP, said the government is looking to find the best approach for the upgrades at HSA.
“For now, the projects are ongoing. However, there are challenges when it comes to upgrading the hospital’s main wing.
“We want to ensure that HSA’s services to the community can continue with minimal disruptions,” he said.
HSA serves as south Johor’s primary government medical referral centre. It accommodates more than 2,000 patients daily, with 1,203 beds.
The hospital started its early operations in 1882 as the region’s first early district hospital. The current iconic five-storey red-brick building along was built later in 1938 to replace that original site.
On the overall development of infrastructure development projects in Johor, Akmal Nasrullah said that since 2000, there have been 613 development projects implemented in the state involving a value of RM56.12 billion.
He added that this included 154 new projects and 459 extension projects, with a ceiling expenditure of RM4.95 billion this year.
“The current expenditure in Johor has exceeded half, which is 50.51 per cent as of July, and equates to RM2.5 billion,” he said.

Title: AGC: Nicky Liow made RM10m payment to compound 26 money laundering charges
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 7 — Businessman Liow Soon Hee, better known as Nicky Liow, paid RM10 million to settle money laundering charges after the Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) accepted his representation and withdrew 26 counts against him.
In a statement today, the AGC said the decision was made in accordance with the Attorney General’s discretionary powers under the Federal Constitution following a detailed review of representation letters submitted by Liow’s lawyers, Tetuan Rajpal, Firah & Vishnu, dated December 15, 2022, and April 6, 2023.
Liow had faced 26 charges under Section 4 of the Anti Money Laundering, Anti Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001 (Act 613) at the Shah Alam Sessions Court on April 12, 2022.
The case had been scheduled for hearings on July 6 and 31, August 1 to 3, August 7 to 10, and September 25 to 27, 2023.
Following the representations, the AGC agreed to offer a compound of RM10 million, which Liow accepted and paid on May 29, 2023. The settlement also included the forfeiture of a bond worth RM647,366 and the confiscation of assets seized during investigations.
In line with Section 92 of Act 613, the AGC subsequently withdrew all charges against Liow. On June 15, 2023, the Shah Alam Sessions Court ordered that he be released and acquitted of all counts.
The AGC stressed that the decision was made independently and based on evidence obtained through comprehensive investigation, without external pressure or public sentiment.
It said the process was conducted professionally and with integrity, in accordance with existing laws, to ensure transparency and uphold justice within Malaysia’s legal system.
The statement also referred to an article published by Free Malaysia Today on August 5, 2026, titled “30 CSOs urge AG to explain DNAA for Nicky Liow”, reiterating that Liow was not released without legal action but only after fulfilling all conditions set under the law.

Title: Premises raided as IRB investigates individuals named in Tabung Haji RCI report, discrepancies found
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 7 — The Inland Revenue Board (IRB) has opened investigations into individuals identified in the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH).
In a statement, IRB said a tax risk analysis had found discrepancies between the individuals’ declared income and their asset holdings.
“IRB officers had raided several related premises to gather information, examine documents and verify facts relevant to the investigations.
“IRB wishes to clarify that all reviews and investigations are conducted professionally, with integrity and in accordance with existing tax laws, without prejudice against any party.
“Further action will be determined only after assessing the information and evidence obtained during the review,” it said.
On July 29, the Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (Jakim) published on its website the 211-page RCI report on Tabung Haji’s management and operations between 2014 and 2020. — Bernama

Title: Four charged in Shah Alam court over false Perkeso Daya Kerjaya 2.0 applications
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Aug 7 — Four individuals were charged in the Sessions Court here today over false statements in applications for incentives under the Social Security Organisation’s (Perkeso) Daya Kerjaya 2.0 career programme, dating back to two years ago.
Among them were a father and son, Chong Foo Yon, 75, the owner of a plastic packaging company, and his son, Chong Kok Woo, 51, who pleaded not guilty after the charges were read out separately before Judge Datuk Mohd Nasri Nordin.
Foo Yon is accused of submitting a Daya Kerjaya 2.0 Employee Confirmation Form on behalf of his company to a Perkeso agent at Taman Bukit Serdang, Seri Kembangan, on November 2, 2024.
The document allegedly contained false statements regarding material particulars of importance, with the intention of misleading the principal.
He was charged under Section 18 of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Act 2009, which provides for imprisonment of up to 20 years and a fine of not less than five times the value of the false material particulars, if such value can be ascertained, or RM10,000, whichever is higher.
As for Kok Woo, he is accused of abetting his father in committing the same offence at the same place, on the same date and time.
The charge against him was brought under Section 28(1)(c) of the MACC Act 2009, punishable under Section 24(2), which provides for imprisonment of up to 20 years and a fine of not less than five times the value of the false material particulars, if such value can be ascertained, or RM10,000, whichever is higher.
Meanwhile, before the same court, a director of a consultancy and development training company pleaded not guilty to four charges of submitting documents with false statements for the same incentive application in March 2024.
Four individuals were charged in the Sessions Court here today over false statements in applications for incentives under the Social Security Organisation’s (Perkeso) Daya Kerjaya 2.0 career programme, dating back to two years ago. — Bernama pic
According to the charges, K. Kumaaravelu, 39, is accused of submitting Daya Kerjaya 2.0 Employee Confirmation Forms containing false statements at his company’s premises in Taman Jaya Utama, Telok Panglima Garang, Kuala Langat, on March 14, 15 and 24, 2024.
The charges were brought under Section 18 of the MACC Act 2009 and are punishable under Section 24(2) of the same Act.
In separate proceedings, Kumaaravelu and another director of the company, N.S. Sivakumar, 54, pleaded not guilty to a joint charge of submitting documents with false statements for the same incentive application, involving a wiring and telecommunications company in Pandamaran, Port Klang, on April 28, 2024.
MACC prosecuting officer Muhammad Arif Asyraf Mohd Khairi applied to the court for bail to be set at RM10,000 for all accused except Kumaaravelu, for whom he proposed bail of RM25,000, in addition to further conditions.
The court then allowed the father and son, as well as Sivakumar, to be released on bail of RM10,000 each. Kumaaravelu was granted bail of RM20,000, each with one surety and additional conditions. The next case mention was fixed for Oct, 29.
Foo Yon and Kok Woo were represented by lawyer L.Y. Yong, while Kumaaravelu and Sivakumar were represented by lawyer P. Vishnuvarman. — Bernama

Title: Perikatan and BN in negotiations for Melaka, Hadi says goal remains to ‘unite and save the Malays’
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Aug 7 — PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang today confirmed that preliminary discussions have begun between Perikatan Nasional (PN) and Barisan Nasional (BN) on seat allocations for the upcoming Melaka state election.
According to
New Straits Times
(NST), Hadi said the talks were at an early stage, with further negotiations expected in the weeks ahead.
“The Melaka state assembly has not been dissolved, but discussions, particularly on Malay Muslim unity, are ongoing. PN and BN are working to unite and save the Malays,” he was quoted as saying after Friday prayers in Marang.
He added that the negotiations would take into account the outcome of the last general election, when BN failed to secure any parliamentary seats in Melaka.
His remarks came in response to BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, who recently stated the coalition’s intention to defend 21 of the 28 seats it currently holds in the state.
Separately, Hadi welcomed the inclusion of two PN assemblymen in the Negri Sembilan executive council under Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim.

Title: Anwar extends condolences to family of former CJ Mohamed Eusoff Chin
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 7 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has extended his condolences to the entire family of former Chief Justice Tun Mohamed Eusoff Chin, who died this morning.
In a Facebook post today, Anwar said Mohamed Eusoff had rendered great service to the nation, particularly in strengthening the judicial institution throughout his career.
“His contributions and service will always be remembered.
“May Allah SWT forgive all his sins, shower His mercy upon him, and place his soul among the righteous and the faithful,” he said.
Anwar ended the post with a recitation of Al-Fatihah as a mark of respect to the deceased.
Mohamed Eusoff, 91, was laid to rest at the Section 9 Muslim Cemetery in Kota Damansara.
He served as Malaysia’s second Chief Justice from September 1994 to December 2000. — Bernama

Title: Hannah Yeoh, KL mayor sample Kuching’s culinary scene
Article:
KUCHING, Aug 7 — Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh and Kuala Lumpur Mayor Datuk Seri Fadlun Mak Ujud sampled a taste of Kuching’s culinary scene on Friday morning as part of their visit to the city.
The two, who arrived in Kuching for a series of engagements, began the day with a visit to Kuching South Mayor Dato Wee Hong Seng.
Wee later accompanied them to the Borneo Culinary World Cup (BCWC) 2026 at Chung Hua Primary School No. 3, where they spent the morning touring the competition venue.
Yeoh and Fadlun stopped at several competition areas to watch participants at work and take a closer look at the culinary creations on display.
They also observed the exchange of techniques and ideas among local and international culinary professionals taking part in the event.
The visit offered the two guests a glimpse into Kuching’s growing gastronomy scene before they continued with other engagements in the city later in the day. — The Borneo Post

Title: Sarawak implements Education Ministry’s Child Protection Policy, parents among those required to sign compliance pledge
Article:
KUCHING, Aug 7 — Sarawak began implementing the Ministry of Education’s (MoE) Child Protection Policy (CPP) on July 27, months after the nationwide rollout was announced in January.
Sarawak Education director Omar Mahli said the State Education Department has directed all district education offices to immediately implement the policy after receiving MoE Circulars (SPI) No. 3 and No. 4 of 2026.
“Although an initial briefing on the policy was conducted in early February, its implementation in Sarawak could only proceed after the necessary authority for its implementation was obtained,” he told
The Borneo Post
.
Under the CPP, individuals dealing with students and schools are required to sign a Student Protection Policy Compliance Pledge (Aku Janji), a core component of the policy.
This includes parents, teachers, staff, and all agencies with direct involvement with schools.
Omar said the CPP aims to safeguard the safety, well-being, and rights of students, while protecting them from exploitation by irresponsible parties.
He further explained that the declarations made in the compliance pledge may be used by schools to substantiate or refute any matters or actions, including the circulation or dissemination of incidents within school premises on social media, as stated and agreed upon in the pledge.
“In other words, once an individual signs the Aku Janji, they are expected to honour the commitments outlined in it,” he stressed.
On actions that could be taken against teachers or other signatories found to have breached the pledge, Omar said the details would be explained later this month.
“This will be explained during the briefing by the Daily School Management Section (BPSH) on August 20, 2026, as there are some updates to the policy’s implementation,” he said.
He clarified that members of the public are not prohibited from sharing or circulating incidents involving schools on social media.
“The Aku Janji applies only to individuals or agencies with direct dealings with students and schools,” he said.
He added schools may also share information on incidents taking place within the school premises with parents, and provide a form for parents and visitors to notify the school of any incidents. — The Borneo Post

Title: N. Sembilan MB Ismail Lasim helms finance, security and investment portfolios
Article:
KUALA PILAH, Aug 7 — Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim will lead three major portfolios in the state government administration for the 2026-2031 term, including Islamic Religious Affairs and Security; Finance, Land and Natural Resources; and Investment, Infrastructure, Utilities, Communications and Felda.
The Juasseh state assemblyman also announced the appointment of ten State Government Councilors including retaining two Exco members, namely Datuk Mohd Faizal Ramli (Linggi) and Mustapha Nagoor (Palong).
Mohd Faizal was appointed as the Rural Development and Regional Development Exco, while Mustapha will retain his old portfolio as the Youth and Sports Development Exco.
Ismail said the Exco members were reminded to shoulder the trust given with full responsibility because the task of administering the state requires commitment and determination to ensure that the welfare and interests of the people are maintained.
“I am confident and believe that all ranks are pleased with the Tuanku (Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir) understanding how great our responsibility is to maintain harmony and progress of Negeri Sembilan. It is more important to ensure the well-being of the people who have given us their votes and confidence,” he said.
Meanwhile, he said his party would appoint an officer from the Indian community with Exco status under the Menteri Besar’s Office to ensure that the community also has a role in the state government administration.
“This is to give opportunities to various races (in the state government)...the representative is from MIC and the name of the candidate has been submitted by the party...when appointed) we will decide later in the Exco meeting,” he said, adding that there was no need to appoint a deputy Exco.
He said the state government was also considering the appointment of a representative of the Orang Asli community in the administration and would refer to the Orang Asli Development Department (Jakoa) to find a suitable candidate.
Earlier, all the Exco members were sworn in before the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir at Istana Besar Seri Menanti here.
Also included in the new Exco line-up are Datuk Zaifulbahri Idris (Chembong) holding the Education, Higher Education and Human Capital portfolio, Siow Kong Choon (Chennah) as the Local Government Development, Housing and Non-Muslim Affairs Exco.
Labu assemblyman, Siti Nur Umaira Hasim holding the Women, Family and Community Development portfolio, Datuk Mohd Asna Amin (Lenggeng) was appointed as the Industry, Technology, Innovation and Digital Exco, while Datuk Mohd Razi Mohd Ali (Sungai Lui) was appointed as the Agriculture, Food Security and Cost of Living Exco.
Suhaimizan Bizar (Gemencheh) was appointed as the Health, Unity, Information, National Integration and Non-Governmental Organisations (NGO) Exco.
Meanwhile, the Perikatan Nasional (PN) through Mohd Fairuz Mohd Isa (Serting) holds the portfolio of Entrepreneurship, Human Resources, Climate Change, Cooperatives and Consumerism) and Datuk Razali Abu Samah (Sikamat) was appointed as the Tourism, Arts, Culture and Heritage Exco).
The results of the 16th Negeri Sembilan State Election saw Barisan Nasional (BN) won 18 State Legislative Assembly seats while Perikatan Nasional (PN) won seven seats, thus enabling the two coalitions to form the state government with a two-thirds majority. — Bernama

Title: Three men arrested after leading police on car chase in Sibu
Article:
SIBU, Aug 7 — Three local men were arrested after allegedly leading police on a chase before being detained in Sungai Merah on Friday, with officers also seizing suspected housebreaking tools found inside their vehicle.
Sibu police chief ACP Abang Zainal Abidin Abang Ahmad said the incident occurred at about 1.30am when a Mobile Patrol Vehicle (MPV) team conducting crime prevention patrols spotted a suspicious Toyota Vios at the Paradom roundabout.
“The MPV personnel instructed the driver to stop for inspection, but the vehicle refused to comply and sped off.
“Assistance was immediately sought from other police teams before the vehicle was successfully intercepted along Jalan Lilin in Sungai Merah after a pursuit,” he said in a statement on Friday.
Abang Zainal said three local men were detained for further investigation, while police also seized the car and several items believed to be commonly used for housebreaking, including a bolt cutter and a metal pry tool.
“The suspects were unable to provide a reasonable explanation for possessing the equipment. Investigations are being carried out to determine whether they were linked to any planned criminal activities,” he said.
He added that the case is being investigated under Section 186 of the Penal Code for obstructing a public servant in the discharge of public functions, Section 37 of the Minor Offences Act 1955, and Section 6(1) of the Corrosive and Explosive Substances and Offensive Weapons Act 1958.
The suspects, aged between 28 and 40, have been remanded for four days until Aug 11 to facilitate investigations.
Police are also continuing efforts to determine whether the suspects are connected to other property crime cases in the district. — The Borneo Post

Title: Unsafe George Town heritage properties to be shuttered, MBPP vows strict enforcement on owners
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Aug 7 — The Penang Island City Council (MBPP) is considering engaging qualified engineers to conduct visual inspections of heritage buildings within the George Town World Heritage Site.
MBPP Mayor Datuk A. Rajendran said the city council is also considering introducing a requirement for heritage building owners to submit a structural assessment report to the council every two years.
He said the report is necessary to ensure that their properties remain safe and well maintained.
“The recent incident serves as an important reminder that all owners of heritage properties have a responsibility to carry out periodic inspections and maintenance to preserve the historical significance, structural integrity, and safety of these valuable buildings for future generations,” he said.
He was commenting on a recent incident in which the beam of a pre-war house along Armenian Street collapsed and injured two tourists walking by.
“Owners or occupants should pay close attention to any signs of structural deterioration, including cracks in walls, leaning walls, decayed timber beams, water seepage, roof damage, termite infestation, loose plaster, and any movement or displacement of structural elements,” he said.
He also encouraged property owners and occupants to visit the Department of Heritage Conservation at the Town Hall during office hours to obtain advice and guidance on appropriate conservation methods and maintenance practices.
He said pre-war house owners should carry out regular maintenance of their properties throughout the year.
He added that they should also conduct structural inspections at least once every two years.
“Given the age of these buildings, periodic inspections are essential to identify early signs of deterioration and to ensure the safety of occupants and the public,” he said.
He said MBPP has identified 66 heritage buildings within the George Town World Heritage Site as being poorly maintained.
“Out of that, 63 units are dilapidated buildings,” he said.
Meanwhile, when asked to comment on the issue, state exco for tourism and creative economy Wong Hon Wai said there needs to be more engagement between these building owners and the city council and George Town World Heritage Incorporated (GTWHI).
“Because some of these owners, they may not have the financial means to upgrade,” he said.
He said he has instructed GTWHI to look into providing more assistance to pre-war house owners.
“We need to have advisory, assistance and enforcement all come together to resolve this issue,” he said.
He added that if any of these pre war buildings are found to pose a danger to the public, businesses will not be allowed to continue operating on the premises.
“They will be advised to stop operations until they restore the building,” he said.
On the tourists who were injured in the incident on August 4, he said both are in stable condition.
“The husband has been discharged from hospital while the wife is still being treated in the hospital,” he said.

Title: Serian joins Kuching, Samarahan as unhealthy API readings rise
Article:
KUCHING, Aug 7 — Serian recorded the highest unhealthy reading on the Air Pollutant Index (API) in Sarawak as of noon today, with a reading of 162.
According to data from the Department of Environment’s Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), this was followed by Samarahan at 140 and Kuching at 139.
Three districts in Sarawak are now recording unhealthy API readings, consisting of Serian, Samarahan and Kuching.
Other districts in Sarawak records moderate readings, ranging from 57 to 91.
An API reading between 101 and 200 is categorised as unhealthy and may pose health risks to sensitive groups, including children, the elderly, and individuals with respiratory conditions. — The Borneo Post

Title: Hadi says Bersatu no longer part of Perikatan after plans for new coalition
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 7 — PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang has claimed that Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu) is no longer a member of Perikatan Nasional (PN) after the party announced plans to form a new political coalition.
Free Malaysia Today (FMT) reported that Abdul Hadi said the PN constitution provides that any party choosing to join or establish another alliance would automatically cease to be a member of the coalition.
“They (Bersatu) have already stated their intention to want to form another ‘team’. They announced it themselves. They are automatically out,” he told reporters after delivering a sermon at Masjid Rusila in Terengganu today.
Abdul Hadi said there was no need for PN to issue a formal announcement on Bersatu’s status as the party had effectively removed itself from the coalition through its stated plans.
“There is no need for an official announcement. They have removed themselves by (making such an announcement),” he said.
The remarks came after PAS ended its political cooperation with Bersatu last month, although both parties remained component members of PN amid growing tensions between the two allies.
Bersatu had previously maintained that it was still part of PN, saying the coalition’s constitution required consensus among all component parties before any member could be removed.
Bersatu president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin had also announced that the party would work with several other parties to form a stronger new coalition following the Negeri Sembilan state election.
He said the proposed coalition would include parties under Ikatan Prihatin Rakyat (IPR), including Parti Putra led by Datuk Ibrahim Ali and Urimai led by P Ramasamy, and would contest the next general election.
